question: What did the voice from heaven declare at Jesus' baptism?
options: 'This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased'
explanation: A voice came from heaven, saying: 'This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.'

question: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before being tempted by the devil?
explanation: And when He had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward He was hungry.

question: How did Jesus answer Satan's first temptation to turn stones into bread?
options: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'
explanation: Jesus quoted Scripture: 'It is written, "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God."'

question: What profession were Peter and his brother Andrew practicing when Jesus called them saying 'Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men'?
explanation: Jesus saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

question: What is the famous opening section of Jesus' Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5 called?
explanation: The Beatitudes are the eight blessings spoken by Jesus beginning with 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.'

question: In the Sermon on the Mount, what two everyday metaphors did Jesus use to describe His followers' influence in the world?
options: Salt of the earth and light of the world
explanation: Jesus told His disciples: 'You are the salt of the earth' and 'You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.'

question: What model prayer did Jesus give His disciples in Matthew 6:9-13?
explanation: Jesus taught His disciples to pray: 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.'

question: What is commonly called 'The Golden Rule' spoken by Jesus in Matthew 7:12?
options: 'Eye for an eye and tooth for tooth'
'Whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them'
'He who has the gold makes the rules'
explanation: 'Therefore, whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.'

question: What was Matthew's occupation before he left everything to follow Jesus?
explanation: As Jesus passed on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office. And He said to him, 'Follow Me.' So he arose and followed Him.

question: How many apostles did Jesus officially choose and send out in Matthew 10 and Luke 6?
explanation: Jesus called His twelve disciples to Him and gave them power over unclean spirits and to heal all kinds of sickness.

question: What Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin came to speak with Jesus privately at night in John 3?
explanation: Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night and was told: 'Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.'

question: What famous verse in the New Testament declares: 'For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son'?
explanation: 'For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.'

question: At Jacob's well in Sychar, to whom did Jesus reveal that He was the Messiah who offers 'living water'?
explanation: Jesus spoke with the Samaritan woman about true worship in spirit and truth, and openly declared to her: 'I who speak to you am He.'

question: What short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree in Jericho to see Jesus passing by?
explanation: Zacchaeus was of small stature and ran ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see Jesus, who called him down and stayed at his house.

question: What blind beggar cried out loudly, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' outside Jericho and received his sight?
explanation: Blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the road begging; Jesus called him and said, 'Go your way; your faith has made you well.'

question: In John 11:35, what is the shortest verse in the English Bible?
explanation: When Jesus saw Mary weeping at the tomb of her brother Lazarus, 'Jesus wept.'

question: How long had Lazarus been dead in the tomb before Jesus called him forth in Bethany?
explanation: Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days, and Martha warned that there would be a stench, yet Jesus cried: 'Lazarus, come forth!'

question: What animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday to fulfill the prophecy of Zechariah 9:9?
explanation: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey's colt, fulfilling prophecy: 'Behold, your King is coming to you, lowly, and sitting on a donkey.'

question: What word of praise, meaning 'Save now!', did the crowds shout as they spread palm branches before Jesus?
explanation: The multitudes cried out: 'Hosanna to the Son of David! "Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD!" Hosanna in the highest!'

question: What did Jesus overturn when He cleansed the Temple of Jerusalem of corrupt commerce?
options: The tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves
explanation: Jesus drove out all who bought and sold in the temple, saying, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves.'

question: According to Jesus in Matthew 22:37-39, what is the greatest commandment in the Law?
options: 'You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind'
'You shall tithe of all your income'
explanation: Jesus declared the first and great commandment: 'You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.'

question: How much money did the poor widow put into the Temple treasury that Jesus commended above all the rich contributors?
options: Two mites (copper coins), which make a quadrans
explanation: The poor widow put in two mites; Jesus remarked that she put in more than all the rest because she gave all her livelihood out of her poverty.

question: For how many pieces of silver did Judas Iscariot agree to betray Jesus to the chief priests?
explanation: The chief priests weighed out thirty pieces of silver for Judas, fulfilling the prophecy of Zechariah 11:12.

question: What humble act of service did Jesus perform for His disciples before the Last Supper in John 13?
options: He gave them gifts of gold
He anointed their heads with perfume
explanation: Jesus poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet, teaching them that true greatness is found in servant leadership.

question: In John 14:6, what exclusive claim did Jesus make about Himself?
options: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me'
explanation: Jesus said to Thomas: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.'

question: In what garden did Jesus agonize in prayer before His arrest, praying: 'Father, if it is Your will, take this cup away from Me; nevertheless not My will, but Yours, be done'?
explanation: In Gethsemane on the Mount of Olives, Jesus knelt and prayed in agony, and His sweat became like great drops of blood falling to the ground.

question: What sign did Judas use in the garden to identify Jesus to the arresting mob?
explanation: Judas had given them a sign: 'Whomever I kiss, He is the One; seize Him.' He immediately went up to Jesus and said, 'Greetings, Rabbi!' and kissed Him.

question: Whose right ear did Peter cut off with a sword during Jesus' arrest, which Jesus immediately touched and healed?
options: Malchus, the servant of the high priest
explanation: Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear; his name was Malchus, and Jesus touched his ear and healed him.

question: How many times did Peter deny knowing Jesus before the rooster crowed, just as Jesus had predicted?
explanation: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times in the high priest's courtyard, and immediately the rooster crowed, and Peter went out and wept bitterly.

question: Who was the Roman governor of Judea who sentenced Jesus to be crucified despite declaring three times 'I find no fault in Him'?
explanation: Pontius Pilate repeatedly declared Jesus innocent, yet to appease the crowd, he washed his hands and delivered Jesus to be crucified.

question: What notorious prisoner and murderer did the crowd demand that Pilate release instead of Jesus?
explanation: The chief priests and elders persuaded the multitudes to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.

question: What was placed on Jesus' head by Roman soldiers to mock His royal claim?
explanation: When they had twisted a crown of thorns, they put it on His head, and a reed in His right hand, and mocked Him saying, 'Hail, King of the Jews!'

question: What man from Cyrene in North Africa was compelled by Roman soldiers to bear Jesus' cross behind Him?
explanation: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; him they compelled to bear His cross.

question: What place, meaning 'The Place of a Skull' (Calvary), was the site where Jesus was crucified?
explanation: They came to a place called Golgotha, which is to say, Place of a Skull (in Latin, Calvary).

question: What words did Jesus speak on the cross concerning His executioners in Luke 23:34?
options: 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do'
explanation: Jesus prayed from the cross: 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do.'

question: What promise did Jesus make from the cross to the penitent thief who asked Jesus to remember him?
options: 'Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise'
explanation: Jesus said to him, 'Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.'

question: What was Jesus' triumphant sixth cry on the cross recorded in John 19:30, signaling redemption's completion?
explanation: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, 'It is finished!' And bowing His head, He gave up His spirit.

question: What happened to the heavy veil of the Temple at the exact moment Jesus died?
options: It was torn in two from top to bottom
It fell to the floor intact
explanation: Then, behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, signifying that access to God's presence was opened to all.

question: What wealthy member of the Sanhedrin asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and buried Him in his own new rock-hewn tomb?
explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich disciple of Jesus, went to Pilate, asked for the body of Jesus, and laid it in his own new tomb cut out of the rock.

question: Who was the first person to encounter the resurrected Jesus in the garden on Sunday morning in John 20?
explanation: Mary Magdalene stood weeping outside the tomb; Jesus appeared to her and called her by name: 'Mary!' She turned and said, 'Rabboni!'

question: Which apostle doubted the reports of Jesus' resurrection until he saw the nail prints and touched Jesus' side?
explanation: Thomas said, 'Unless I see in His hands the print of the nails... I will not believe.' When Jesus appeared, Thomas exclaimed, 'My Lord and my God!'

question: To what village were two disciples traveling on resurrection afternoon when the risen Jesus walked with them unrecognized?
explanation: Two disciples were traveling to a village named Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem, when Jesus Himself drew near and went with them.

question: How many times did the risen Jesus ask Peter, 'Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?' by the Sea of Galilee to reinstate him?
explanation: Jesus asked Peter three times, corresponding to Peter's three denials, each time commanding him: 'Feed My lambs / Tend My sheep.'

question: What is the Great Commission given by Jesus to His disciples in Matthew 28:19-20?
options: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'
explanation: Jesus commanded: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them... and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.'

question: What elderly prophetess in the Temple of Jerusalem recognized baby Jesus as the Redeemer and gave thanks to God?
explanation: Anna, a prophetess of the tribe of Asher, lived in the temple serving God with fastings and prayers; she spoke of Jesus to all who looked for redemption.

question: What elderly righteous man took baby Jesus into his arms in the Temple and declared the song known as the 'Nunc Dimittis'?
explanation: Simeon took Jesus in his arms, saying, 'Lord, now You are letting Your servant depart in peace, according to Your word; for my eyes have seen Your salvation.'

question: How old was Jesus when His parents found Him sitting in the midst of the teachers in the Jerusalem Temple?
explanation: When He was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem, and after three days found Him in the temple listening and asking questions.

question: What was Jesus' answer to Mary when she found Him in the Temple at age 12?
options: 'Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?'
explanation: Jesus said to them: 'Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?'

question: What was John the Baptist's unusual diet while ministering in the wilderness of Judea?
explanation: John was clothed in camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist; and his food was locusts and wild honey.

question: Who was the Roman emperor when John the Baptist began his public ministry in the 15th year of his reign (Luke 3:1)?
explanation: Luke precisely anchors John's ministry: 'In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea...'

question: What exclamation did Nathanael make to Philip when Philip first told him they had found the Messiah from Nazareth?
options: 'Can anything good come out of Nazareth?'
explanation: Nathanael said to Philip, 'Can anything good come out of Nazareth?' Philip answered, 'Come and see.'

question: What did Jesus say to Nathanael that amazed him and convinced him of Jesus' omniscience and messiahship?
options: 'Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you'
explanation: Jesus answered: 'Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.' Nathanael replied: 'Rabbi, You are the Son of God!'

question: In which synagogue did Jesus read from the scroll of Isaiah 61 and announce: 'Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing', leading His hometown to try to throw Him off a cliff?
explanation: In His hometown of Nazareth, the people were filled with wrath when Jesus proclaimed fulfillment of Isaiah and led Him to the brow of the hill to throw Him down.

question: What city on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee served as the primary headquarters for Jesus' Galilean ministry?
explanation: Leaving Nazareth, Jesus came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is by the sea, often called 'His own city.'

question: What did the Roman centurion in Capernaum say that caused Jesus to marvel and say He had not found such great faith in all Israel?
options: 'Only speak a word, and my servant will be healed'
explanation: The centurion understood authority: 'Lord, I am not worthy that You should come under my roof. But only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.'

question: How did four friends get a paralyzed man to Jesus in Capernaum when the house was completely packed with a crowd?
options: They pushed through the front door
They dug through the roof and lowered the man down on his bed
explanation: When they could not come near Him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where He was and let down the bed on which the paralytic lay.

question: Why did the religious leaders accuse Jesus of blasphemy when He spoke to the paralyzed man let down through the roof?
options: Because He healed on the Sabbath
Because He said, 'Son, your sins are forgiven you'
Because He didn't wash His hands
explanation: The scribes reasoned in their hearts: 'Why does this Man speak blasphemies like this? Who can forgive sins but God alone?'

question: What nickname did Jesus give to the brothers James and John, the sons of Zebedee?
explanation: James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James He surnamed Boanerges, which means 'Sons of Thunder.'

question: Who were the three apostles in Jesus' inner circle who accompanied Him to the Transfiguration, the raising of Jairus's daughter, and Gethsemane?
explanation: Peter, James, and John were the inner three apostles chosen to witness Christ's greatest glories and deepest sorrows.

question: What two Old Testament figures appeared talking with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration?
explanation: Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared in glory and spoke of Christ's decease at Jerusalem.

question: What was Peter's impulsive suggestion while witnessing the Transfiguration on the mount?
options: To build three tabernacles (booths)—one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah
To call down fire from heaven
explanation: Peter said to Jesus: 'Lord, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tabernacles: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.'

question: At Caesarea Philippi, what was Peter's famous answer when Jesus asked: 'Who do you say that I am?'
options: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God'
'You are John the Baptist risen from the dead'
'You are the King of the Jews'
explanation: Simon Peter answered and said: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'

question: Why did Jesus rebuke Peter sharply in Matthew 16:23 saying 'Get behind Me, Satan!' right after praising him?
options: Peter tried to rebuke Jesus for prophesying His death and resurrection
explanation: When Peter took Jesus aside and objected to His upcoming crucifixion, Jesus said: 'Get behind Me, Satan! You are an offense to Me, for you are not mindful of the things of God.'

question: Which Roman tetrarch executed John the Baptist by beheading after dancing at his birthday banquet?
explanation: Herod Antipas beheaded John in prison because of an oath he made to Salome, the daughter of Herodias, who danced before him.

question: Why had John the Baptist been imprisoned by Herod Antipas in the first place?
options: For rebuking Herod for marrying Herodias, his brother Philip's wife
For preaching baptism without a license
explanation: John had courageously confronted Herod, saying: 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.'

question: In John 6, following the feeding of the 5,000, what profound title did Jesus declare of Himself that caused many disciples to turn back?
explanation: Jesus declared: 'I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger.' Many stumbled when He spoke of eating His flesh and drinking His blood.

question: When many disciples walked away from Jesus in John 6, what was Peter's steadfast response when Jesus asked the twelve if they would go away too?
options: 'Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life'
'We will stay if the others stay'
'We do not know what to do'
explanation: Simon Peter answered: 'Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'

question: What two sisters hosted Jesus in their home in Bethany, where one sat at Jesus' feet listening while the other was distracted with much serving?
explanation: Martha was distracted with much serving, while Mary sat at Jesus' feet; Jesus commended Mary for choosing that good part.

question: What did Mary of Bethany do with an alabaster flask of very costly spikenard oil days before the crucifixion?
options: Sold it to feed the poor
Poured it on Jesus' head and feet and wiped His feet with her hair
Offered it to the temple treasury
explanation: Mary anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair; Jesus explained that she had kept this oil for the day of His burial.

question: Who complained that Mary's perfume should have been sold for 300 denarii and given to the poor, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief?
explanation: Judas Iscariot objected to the cost of the perfume; John records that Judas was a thief and held the money box, stealing from it.

question: What did Jesus say would be remembered wherever the gospel was preached throughout the whole world?
options: What this woman (Mary of Bethany) had done in anointing Him
The feeding of the five thousand
explanation: 'Assuredly, I say to you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told as a memorial to her.'

question: What Jewish feast was Jesus celebrating with His disciples during the Last Supper in the Upper Room?
explanation: Jesus said to them: 'With fervent desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.'

question: What new commandment did Jesus give to His disciples in John 13:34?
options: 'That you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another'
explanation: 'A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples.'

question: In John 15, what metaphor did Jesus use to describe the vital relationship between Himself and His followers?
options: I am the True Vine, and you are the branches
explanation: 'I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.'

question: What title did Jesus use for the Holy Spirit in John 14:16, 26 and 16:7?
explanation: Jesus promised: 'I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever—the Spirit of truth.'

question: What high priest presided over the Sanhedrin trial that condemned Jesus for blasphemy?
explanation: High Priest Caiaphas tore his clothes and declared: 'He has spoken blasphemy! What further need do we have of witnesses?'

question: What was the tragic end of Judas Iscariot after he saw that Jesus was condemned?
options: He threw the 30 silver pieces into the temple and went and hanged himself
explanation: Judas was seized with remorse, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, threw them down in the temple, and departed and hanged himself.

question: What was the potter's field bought with Judas's returned blood money called in Aramaic?
explanation: The chief priests bought with the money the potter's field to bury strangers in, which became known as Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.

question: What warning did Pilate's wife send to him while he was sitting on the judgment seat?
options: 'Have nothing to do with that just Man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of Him'
explanation: Pilate's wife sent a message urging him: 'Have nothing to do with that just Man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of Him.'

question: What inscription was placed above Jesus' head on the cross in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin?
options: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS' (INRI)
explanation: Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS', written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.

question: What did Roman soldiers do with Jesus' seamless tunic rather than tearing it into pieces?
options: They cast lots for it to decide whose it should be
They threw it into the mud
explanation: They said among themselves, 'Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be,' fulfilling Psalm 22:18.

question: To which disciple did Jesus entrust the care of His mother Mary while hanging on the cross?
explanation: Jesus said to His mother, 'Woman, behold your son!' and to John, 'Behold your mother!' From that hour John took her into his own home.

question: What exclamation did the Roman centurion at the foot of the cross make when he saw how Jesus breathed His last?
options: 'Truly this was the Son of God!'
explanation: When the centurion and those with him saw the earthquake and the things that happened, they feared greatly, saying: 'Truly this was the Son of God!'

question: What mixture of spices, weighing about 100 pounds, did Nicodemus bring to prepare Jesus' body for burial?
explanation: Nicodemus came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds, and they bound Jesus' body in linen strips with the spices.

question: Why did the chief priests ask Pilate to secure and seal Jesus' tomb with a Roman guard until the third day?
options: To prevent grave robbers from taking spices
Lest His disciples steal the body and claim He rose from the dead
Out of respect for the Sabbath
explanation: They said, 'Sir, we remember while He was still alive, how that deceiver said, "After three days I will rise." Therefore command that the tomb be made secure.'

question: What happened when the angel of the Lord descended from heaven at the resurrection in Matthew 28:2?
options: There was a great earthquake, and the angel rolled back the stone from the door and sat on it
explanation: Behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat on it.

question: What angel message did the women hear at the empty tomb on Sunday morning?
options: 'Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for He is risen, as He said.'
explanation: The angel said: 'Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.'

question: What false cover story did the chief priests pay the Roman soldiers a large bribe of money to circulate?
options: 'His disciples came at night and stole Him away while we slept'
explanation: They gave a large sum of money to the soldiers, telling them to say, 'His disciples came at night and stole Him away while we slept.'

question: What was the name of one of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus whose heart burned within him as Jesus opened the Scriptures?
explanation: The one whose name was Cleopas answered Him; and later they said, 'Did not our heart burn within us while He talked with us on the road?'

question: At what exact moment did the two Emmaus disciples finally recognize the risen Jesus?
options: When He walked up to them
When He took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them
explanation: As He sat at the table with them, He took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened and they knew Him; and He vanished from their sight.

question: What food did the risen Jesus eat in the presence of His terrified disciples in Luke 24 to prove He was physically bodily alive and not a ghost?
options: A piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb
explanation: Jesus said, 'Have you any food here?' So they gave Him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb, and He took it and ate in their presence.

question: How many large fish were caught when the risen Jesus directed the disciples to cast their net on the right side of the boat in John 21?
explanation: Simon Peter went up and dragged the net to land, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three; and although there were so many, the net was not broken.

question: From what location near Jerusalem did Jesus ascend into heaven forty days after His resurrection?
explanation: Jesus led them out as far as Bethany, lifted up His hands, and blessed them; while He blessed them, He was parted from them and carried up into heaven from the Mount of Olives.

question: According to the final verse of the Gospel of John (John 21:25), how many other things did Jesus do?
options: Only what was written in the four Gospels
So many that if every one were written, even the world itself could not contain the books
explanation: 'And there are also many other things that Jesus did, which if they were written one by one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that would be written.'

question: In Luke 1, what priestly division was Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist, serving in when the angel Gabriel appeared to him?
explanation: Zacharias was a priest of the division of Abijah (one of the 24 priestly orders established by King David in 1 Chronicles 24:10).

question: What physical affliction struck Zacharias in the Holy Place because he doubted Gabriel's promise that Elizabeth would bear a son?
options: He became mute and unable to speak until the boy was born and named
explanation: Gabriel declared: 'You will be mute and not able to speak until the day these things take place, because you did not believe my words.'

question: What Latin name is traditionally given to Mary's song of praise in Luke 1:46-55 beginning 'My soul magnifies the Lord'?
explanation: Mary's hymn of praise is called the Magnificat from its opening word in the Latin Vulgate ('Magnificat anima mea Dominum').

question: What Latin name is traditionally given to Zacharias's prophetic song of praise in Luke 1:68-79 upon the naming of John?
explanation: Zacharias's hymn is called the Benedictus from its opening Latin words: 'Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel' ('Blessed be the Lord God of Israel').

question: Who was the Roman governor of Syria during the worldwide census decreed by Caesar Augustus at the time of Jesus' birth (Luke 2:2)?
explanation: Luke writes: 'This census first took place while Quirinius was governing Syria.'

question: In Matthew 1, how many total generations are structured in the genealogy from Abraham to David, David to the Babylonian captivity, and from captivity to Christ?
explanation: Matthew highlights a symmetric structure: fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the captivity, and fourteen to Christ.

question: What four unusual women (outside Mary) are explicitly mentioned in Matthew's royal genealogy of Jesus?
options: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah (Bathsheba)
explanation: Matthew exceptionally highlights Tamar, Rahab the Canaanite, Ruth the Moabitess, and Bathsheba (Uriah's wife), emphasizing God's grace to all.

question: In John 1:1, what profound theological Greek term translated 'the Word' is used for the pre-existent Son of God who was with God and was God?
explanation: 'In the beginning was the Word (Logos), and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.'

question: In John 2, how many stone waterpots used for Jewish purification rites did Jesus order filled with water at the wedding in Cana?
explanation: There were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of purification of the Jews, containing twenty or thirty gallons apiece.

question: What pool in Jerusalem with five porches was the site where Jesus healed a man who had an infirmity for 38 years on the Sabbath?
explanation: By the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem was a pool called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches, where an angel occasionally stirred the waters.

question: What pool in Jerusalem, whose name means 'Sent', did Jesus send the man born blind to wash in after anointing his eyes with mud and saliva?
explanation: Jesus said to the blind man: 'Go, wash in the pool of Siloam' (which is translated, Sent). So he went and washed, and came back seeing.

question: In Luke 10:1, how many disciples (in addition to the twelve apostles) did Jesus commission and send out two by two ahead of Him into every city?
explanation: The Lord appointed seventy others also, and sent them two by two before His face into every city and place where He Himself was about to go.

question: Which of the twelve apostles was also called Nathanael in the Gospel of John?
explanation: Bartholomew (meaning 'Son of Tolmai') is consistently paired with Philip in the synoptic lists, corresponding to Nathanael in John.

question: What apostle is also designated as Judas the son (or brother) of James and was surnamed Thaddaeus or Lebbaeus?
explanation: Thaddaeus is identified in Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13 as 'Judas the son of James' (clarified in John 14:22 as 'Judas, not Iscariot').

question: What political party or background did the apostle Simon belong to before following Jesus, known for passionate opposition to Rome?
explanation: Simon is designated 'the Zealot' (Greek 'Zelotes', Aramaic 'Cananaean'), indicating previous affiliation with Jewish nationalist freedom fighters.

question: What question did the disciples of John the Baptist bring to Jesus from Machaerus prison in Matthew 11:3?
options: 'Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?'
explanation: John sent two of his disciples to ask: 'Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?' Jesus pointed to His miracles of healing and gospel preaching.

question: What Hebrew word of supreme insult or contempt did Jesus warn against speaking to a brother in Matthew 5:22?
explanation: Jesus warned: 'Whoever says to his brother, "Raca!" shall be in danger of the council. But whoever says, "You fool!" shall be in danger of hell fire.'

question: What Jewish tradition of declaring property dedicated to God to avoid supporting elderly parents was condemned by Jesus as making God's word void?
explanation: The scribes said that if a man told his father or mother, 'Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban' (a gift to God), he was exempt from helping them.

question: What unique title is used by Jesus throughout the Gospels more than 80 times to refer to Himself, reflecting Daniel 7:13?
explanation: 'The Son of Man' was Jesus' favorite self-designation, emphasizing both His genuine humanity and His heavenly apocalyptic authority from Daniel 7.

question: In Luke 13:32, what animal did Jesus call King Herod Antipas when Pharisees warned that Herod wanted to kill Him?
explanation: Jesus said to them: 'Go, tell that fox, "Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected."'

question: Which Jewish party in Jesus' day rejected the resurrection of the dead, angels, and spirits?
explanation: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection—and no angel or spirit; they posed the hypothetical question about the woman with seven brothers.

question: What was Jesus' devastating response to the Sadducees regarding the woman who married seven brothers in Matthew 22:29-32?
options: 'You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage'
explanation: Jesus declared that God is not the God of the dead, but of the living ('I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob').

question: In John 8:58, what absolute divine name did Jesus use of Himself that led the religious authorities to pick up stones to stone Him?
explanation: Jesus said to them, 'Most assuredly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I AM.' They took up stones because He claimed the divine covenant name of God.

question: In John 10:22, during what winter festival celebrating the rededication of the Temple (Hanukkah) did Jesus walk in Solomon's Porch?
explanation: 'Now it was the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon's porch.'

question: What high priest was the father-in-law of Caiaphas to whom Jesus was first led immediately after His arrest in Gethsemane?
explanation: They led Jesus away to Annas first, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas who was high priest that year, wielding immense behind-the-scenes power.

question: What did Caiaphas prophesy unconsciously before the Sanhedrin in John 11:49-50 regarding Jesus' death?
options: 'It is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and not that the whole nation should perish'
explanation: Being high priest that year, Caiaphas prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and not for that nation only, but to gather the scattered children of God.

question: What Aramaic question of forsakenness did Jesus cry out from the cross at the ninth hour, quoting Psalm 22:1?
options: 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' ('My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?')
explanation: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice: 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' that is, 'My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?'

question: What did the Roman soldiers offer Jesus on the cross when He said 'I thirst'?
options: Sour wine (vinegar) on a sponge put on a hyssop branch
Pure wine mixed with sweet spices
explanation: They filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on hyssop, and put it to His mouth, fulfilling Psalm 69:21.

question: According to John 19:31-37, why did the Roman soldiers not break Jesus' legs as they did to the two thieves?
options: Because they saw that He was already dead, fulfilling 'Not one of His bones shall be broken'
explanation: When they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs, fulfilling Scripture regarding the Passover Lamb.

question: What flowed out immediately when one of the soldiers pierced Jesus' side with a spear?
explanation: One of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out, confirming physical death and theological cleansing.

question: In Matthew 27:52-53, what supernatural occurrence took place in Jerusalem after Jesus' resurrection?
options: The sun never set for three days
Graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised and appeared to many
Fire fell from heaven on the Sanhedrin
explanation: The graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised, and coming out of the graves after His resurrection, they went into the holy city.

question: What stone pavement where Pilate sat on his judgment seat is called in Hebrew (Aramaic) 'Gabbatha'?
explanation: Pilate brought Jesus out and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called The Pavement, but in Hebrew, Gabbatha.

question: In Luke 23:7-11, to which ruler did Pilate send Jesus upon learning He was a Galilean within that ruler's jurisdiction?
explanation: As soon as Pilate knew that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod Antipas, who was also in Jerusalem at that time.

question: What was Jesus' response to Herod Antipas when Herod questioned Him with many words hoping to see a miracle?
explanation: Herod questioned Him with many words, but Jesus answered him nothing, fulfilling Isaiah 53:7: 'He opened not His mouth.'

question: In John 20:17, what did the risen Jesus tell Mary Magdalene when she clung to Him?
options: 'Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; but go to My brethren'
explanation: Jesus said to her, 'Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; but go to My brethren and say to them, "I am ascending to My Father and your Father."'

question: How many days did Jesus appear to His disciples between His resurrection and His ascension (Acts 1:3)?
explanation: Jesus presented Himself alive after His suffering by many infallible proofs, being seen by them during forty days and speaking of things pertaining to the kingdom of God.

question: In Matthew 17:24-27, what miraculous way did Jesus tell Peter to obtain money to pay the two-drachma temple tax for both of them?
options: Cast a hook into the sea, open the mouth of the first fish caught, and find a stater (four-drachma coin)
explanation: Jesus said: 'Go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the fish that comes up first. And when you have opened its mouth, you will find a piece of money; take that and give it to them for Me and you.'

question: In Luke 17:11-19, of the ten lepers healed by Jesus, how many returned to fall at His feet giving thanks?
options: Only one, and he was a Samaritan
explanation: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, returned, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at His feet, giving Him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.

question: What Aramaic word did Jesus use when looking up to heaven and touching a deaf-mute man's ears and tongue in Mark 7:34, meaning 'Be opened'?
explanation: Looking up to heaven, He sighed, and said to him, 'Ephphatha,' that is, 'Be opened.' Immediately his ears were opened and the impediment of his tongue was loosed.

question: What Aramaic words did Jesus speak when raising Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter from the dead in Mark 5:41, meaning 'Little girl, I say to you, arise'?
explanation: He took the child by the hand, and said to her, 'Talitha, cumi,' which is translated, 'Little girl, I say to you, arise.' Immediately the girl arose and walked.

question: In Luke 7:36-50, at whose house was Jesus dining when a weeping sinful woman washed His feet with tears and wiped them with her hair?
explanation: Jesus was dining in the house of Simon the Pharisee, who questioned Jesus' prophetic insight because He allowed the sinful woman to touch Him.

question: What two brothers asked Jesus through their mother Salome for the seats of honor on His right and left hand in His kingdom?
explanation: The mother of Zebedee's sons asked that James and John sit on His right and left hand; Jesus replied that to sit there was for those for whom it has been prepared by His Father.

question: What did Jesus say was the only sign that would be given to the hypocritical generation seeking a sign from heaven?
options: The sign of the prophet Jonah (three days and nights in the fish, as Son of Man in the heart of the earth)
explanation: 'No sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.'

question: What sin did Jesus warn is eternal and will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come?
options: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (attributing the Holy Spirit's divine works to Satan)
explanation: When the scribes claimed Jesus cast out demons by Beelzebub, Jesus warned that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

question: In Luke 18:8, what searching question did Jesus ask regarding His return to earth?
options: 'When the Son of Man comes, will He really find faith on the earth?'
explanation: Concluding the parable of the persistent widow, Jesus asked: 'Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He really find faith on the earth?'

question: In John 7:37-38, on the last and great day of the Feast of Tabernacles, what did Jesus cry aloud to the crowd?
options: 'If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink. He who believes in Me... out of his heart will flow rivers of living water'
explanation: On the great day of the water-drawing ceremony, Jesus stood and cried out that whoever believes in Him, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water, speaking of the Holy Spirit.

question: What did Jesus write on the ground when the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery to test Him in John 8?
options: Scripture does not state what He wrote with His finger on the ground
explanation: John 8:6, 8 records that Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with His finger as though He did not hear, but the exact text is not revealed.

question: What famous challenge did Jesus present to the accusers of the woman caught in adultery in John 8:7?
options: 'He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first'
explanation: When they continued asking Him, He raised Himself up and said to them: 'He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first.'

question: In Luke 19:41-44, why did Jesus weep as He approached Jerusalem on Palm Sunday?
options: Because Jerusalem did not know the time of her visitation, and would be besieged and leveled by enemies
explanation: Jesus wept over Jerusalem, prophesying that days would come when enemies would build an embankment, surround her, and level her to the ground because she did not know the time of her visitation.

question: According to Matthew 26:30 and Mark 14:26, what did Jesus and His disciples do immediately before going out to the Mount of Olives?
options: They sang a hymn (traditionally the Passover Hallel Psalms)
explanation: 'And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.' In Jewish Passover liturgy, the closing hymn consisted of the Great Hallel (Psalms 115–118).

question: Who was the first woman created by God, formed from Adam's rib?
explanation: Adam called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.

question: Who built a massive wooden ark to preserve his family and animals from the worldwide flood?
explanation: God said to Noah: 'Make yourself an ark of gopherwood; make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and outside with pitch.'

question: Who is revered as the 'Father of the Faithful' with whom God made a covenant to bless all nations?
explanation: God told Abram: 'Your name shall be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.'

question: Who was Abraham's wife who gave birth to Isaac in her extreme old age (age 90)?
explanation: Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken.

question: Who was Abraham's miracle son who was bound on an altar on Mount Moriah before God provided a ram?
explanation: Abraham bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar; then God stopped him and provided a ram caught in a thicket.

question: Which twin brother sold his birthright for a single bowl of red lentil stew?
explanation: Esau said, 'Look, I am about to die; so what is this birthright to me?' and he sold his birthright to Jacob.

question: Which of Jacob's twelve sons was thrown into a pit by his brothers and sold into Egypt?
explanation: Joseph's brothers stripped him of his coat of many colors, cast him into a pit, and sold him to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver.

question: Who was the Hebrew prophet chosen by God to lead Israel out of Egyptian slavery and receive the Law?
explanation: God said to Moses at the burning bush: 'Come now, therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh that you may bring My people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.'

question: Who served as Moses' spokesman and became the first High Priest of Israel?
explanation: God appointed Aaron the Levite as Moses' mouth and prophet, later designating him the first High Priest.

question: Who led the Israelites across the Jordan River into the Promised Land after the death of Moses?
explanation: The LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant: 'Moses My servant is dead. Now therefore, arise, go over this Jordan, you and all this people.'

question: Which judge of Israel possessed extraordinary supernatural strength and tore apart a young lion with his bare hands?
explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson, and he tore the young lion apart as one would have torn apart a young goat.

question: What Philistine woman repeatedly enticed Samson until he revealed the secret of his strength?
explanation: Delilah pestered Samson daily with her words until his soul was vexed to death and he told her all his heart.

question: Which young shepherd boy from Bethlehem defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone?
explanation: David prevailed over the Philistine Goliath with a sling and a stone, struck the Philistine, and killed him.

question: Who was the first king of Israel, who stood head and shoulders taller than any of the people?
explanation: Saul son of Kish was a handsome choice young man; from his shoulders upward he was taller than any of the people.

question: Who was King Saul's eldest son who forged a covenant of deep brotherly friendship with David?
explanation: Jonathan made a covenant with David, stripped himself of his royal robe and armor, and gave them to David.

question: Which son of King David was renowned as the wisest and richest king of Israel and authored thousands of proverbs?
explanation: God gave Solomon wisdom and exceedingly great understanding; he spoke three thousand proverbs and his songs were one thousand and five.

question: Who was the fearless prophet who called down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel and was taken to heaven in a whirlwind?
explanation: Elijah the Tishbite proved that Yahweh is the true God on Mount Carmel and was carried to heaven in a fiery chariot.

question: Who was Elijah's dedicated disciple and successor who received a double portion of his spirit?
explanation: Elisha picked up the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him, struck the Jordan waters, and performed twice as many recorded miracles.

question: Which Jewish prophet served as prime minister in Babylon and was unharmed when thrown into a den of hungry lions?
explanation: Daniel told King Darius: 'My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, so that they have not hurt me.'

question: Which prophet tried to flee from God's presence on a ship to Tarshish and spent three days in the belly of a great fish?
explanation: Jonah fled toward Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, was swallowed by a great fish, and later preached repentance to Nineveh.

question: Who was the Jewish orphan girl raised by her cousin Mordecai who became Queen of Persia and saved her people?
explanation: Esther was brought up by Mordecai her cousin; King Ahasuerus loved Esther more than all the other women and set the royal crown upon her head.

question: Who was the forerunner of Christ who lived in the desert, baptized Jesus in the Jordan, and proclaimed: 'Behold! The Lamb of God'?
explanation: John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea and identified Jesus: 'Behold! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!'

question: Who was the mother of Jesus, blessed among women, who conceived the Son of God by the Holy Spirit?
explanation: The angel Gabriel announced to Mary: 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you... therefore, also, that Holy One who is to be born will be called the Son of God.'

question: Who was the righteous carpenter of Nazareth betrothed to Mary who acted as Jesus' earthly adoptive father?
explanation: Joseph, being a just man, obeyed the angel's instruction to take Mary as his wife and named the child Jesus.

question: Which outspoken apostle was named Simon, given the surname Peter (Cephas, Rock), and walked briefly on water toward Jesus?
explanation: Simon Peter stepped down out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus, before crying 'Lord, save me!' when he saw the wind.

question: Which apostle is called 'the disciple whom Jesus loved' and authored a Gospel, three Epistles, and Revelation?
explanation: The Apostle John, son of Zebedee, reclined next to Jesus at the Last Supper and cared for Mary after the crucifixion.

question: Which apostle betrayed Jesus into the hands of the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver?
explanation: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests and delivered Jesus to them in the Garden of Gethsemane.

question: Who was the Pharisee named Saul of Tarsus who fiercely persecuted Christians before becoming the great Apostle to the Gentiles?
explanation: Saul, also called Paul, was dramatically converted on the Damascus road and became the foremost missionary and letter-writer of the early church.

question: Who was the first person created by God, placed in the Garden of Eden to tend and keep it?
explanation: The LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and put Adam into the garden.

question: Who was the younger brother murdered by his jealous brother Cain in the first homicide in human history?
explanation: Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him because Abel's offering was accepted by God while his own was not.

question: Which of Adam and Eve's sons was born after Abel's death, through whose lineage the godly line continued?
explanation: Eve bore a son and named him Seth, saying, 'For God has appointed another seed for me instead of Abel, whom Cain killed.'

question: Who walked with God in Genesis 5:24 and did not experience death because 'God took him'?
explanation: Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him (Hebrews 11:5).

question: Who was Abraham's nephew who chose to live in the fertile Jordan valley near the wicked city of Sodom?
explanation: Lot lifted his eyes, saw the well-watered plain of Jordan, and pitched his tent even as far as Sodom.

question: Who was Abraham's firstborn son born to Sarah's Egyptian maidservant Hagar?
explanation: Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram named his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.

question: Who was the beautiful woman who drew water for Abraham's servant and his ten camels and became Isaac's wife?
explanation: Rebekah willingly drew water for all the camels, fulfilling the exact prayer sign, and became the wife of Isaac.

question: Which of Laban's daughters did Jacob love so deeply that he served seven years for her, which seemed like only a few days?
explanation: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed only a few days to him because of the love he had for her.

question: Which elder daughter of Laban had delicate ('tender') eyes and was substituted as Jacob's bride under the wedding veil?
explanation: Laban deceived Jacob by giving him his elder daughter Leah first on the wedding night.

question: Who was Jacob's youngest son, born as Rachel died near Bethlehem?
explanation: As Rachel's soul was departing, she called his name Ben-Oni (Son of my sorrow), but his father called him Benjamin (Son of my right hand).

question: Which Egyptian officer of Pharaoh bought Joseph from the slave traders and placed him over his entire household?
explanation: Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, saw that the LORD was with Joseph and made him overseer of his house.

question: Who was Moses' older sister who watched over his ark of bulrushes in the Nile and led Israel in worship after crossing the Red Sea?
explanation: Miriam the prophetess took a timbrel in her hand and all the women went out after her with timbrels and dances singing praise to God.

question: Who was Moses' Midianite wife whom he met at a well after fleeing from Egypt?
explanation: Reuel (Jethro) gave Moses Zipporah his daughter, and she bore him a son named Gershom.

question: Who was Moses' father-in-law, a priest of Midian, who advised Moses to appoint capable leaders over tens, fifties, hundreds, and thousands?
explanation: Jethro observed Moses judging the people alone from morning to evening and advised wise delegation to prevent burnout.

question: Which spy from the tribe of Judah wholly followed the LORD and asked Joshua for Mount Hebron as his inheritance at age 85?
explanation: Caleb declared at age 85: 'As yet I am as strong this day as on the day that Moses sent me... Now therefore, give me this mountain.'

question: What Moabitess widow said to Naomi: 'Where you go I will go, and wherever you lodge I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God, my God'?
explanation: Ruth's classic vow of faithful covenant devotion linked her to the people of Israel and the messianic line.

question: Who was the godly, wealthy landowner in Bethlehem who married Ruth under the law of the kinsman-redeemer?
explanation: Boaz redeemed the inheritance of Elimelech and took Ruth the Moabitess to be his wife.

question: What barren woman wept in the Tabernacle at Shiloh and prayed for a son, promising to dedicate him to the LORD as a Nazirite?
explanation: Hannah was in bitterness of soul and prayed to the LORD; God remembered her, and she gave birth to Samuel.

question: Who was the high priest at Shiloh who initially mistook Hannah for a drunken woman as she prayed silently in her heart?
explanation: Eli watched her mouth; because Hannah spoke in her heart, only her lips moved, so Eli thought she was intoxicated.

question: Which beautiful, intelligent woman pacified David with provisions after her foolish husband Nabal insulted David's men?
explanation: Abigail made haste with food and fell at David's feet, preventing David from shedding blood in revenge against Nabal.

question: Who was the wife of Uriah the Hittite with whom King David committed adultery, later becoming the mother of Solomon?
explanation: David saw Bathsheba the daughter of Eliam bathing from his palace roof and sent messengers to take her.

question: Which queen of a southern nation traveled thousands of miles to Jerusalem with gold, gems, and spices to test Solomon's wisdom?
explanation: When the Queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions.

question: Which of King Saul's daughters was given to David as his first wife after he killed 200 Philistines?
explanation: Saul gave David his daughter Michal as wife because she loved David, though she later despised him when he danced before the Ark.

question: Who was David's fierce and loyal nephew who served as commander of his army throughout almost his entire reign?
explanation: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, a master tactician who ruthlessly defended David's throne.

question: Who was the supreme commander of King Saul's army who later defected to David and was assassinated by Joab at Hebron?
explanation: Abner son of Ner was Saul's general; Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly and stabbed him in the stomach.

question: Who was the Edomite chief herdsman of Saul who obeyed Saul's order to slaughter 85 priests of the LORD at Nob?
explanation: When Saul's servants refused to strike the priests of the LORD, Doeg the Edomite turned and struck eighty-five men who wore a linen ephod.

question: Which sole surviving priest escaped the massacre at Nob and fled to David with the priestly ephod?
explanation: One of the sons of Ahimelech, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David, remaining with him throughout his exile.

question: What wealthy 80-year-old Gileadite provided food, beds, and supplies to King David while he fled from Absalom across the Jordan?
explanation: Barzillai the Gileadite was a very aged man who provided the king with supplies while he stayed at Mahanaim.

question: Who was the Benjamite from the house of Saul who pelted King David with stones and hurled curses at him during his flight from Absalom?
explanation: Shimei cursed continuously as he came from Bahurim and threw stones at David and at all his servants.

question: What deceitful servant of Mephibosheth lied to David, falsely accusing Mephibosheth of seeking Saul's kingdom for himself?
explanation: Ziba brought food to David and slandered his crippled master Mephibosheth to gain ownership of Saul's land.

question: Which of David's sons attempted to seize the throne as David lay dying of old age, supported by Joab and Abiathar?
explanation: Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, 'I will be king', but Nathan and Bathsheba intervened on behalf of Solomon.

question: Who was the young Shunammite virgin chosen to attend to elderly King David and keep him warm in his final days?
explanation: They sought for a lovely young woman and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king to minister to him.

question: Who was Solomon's foolish son whose harsh words ('My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scourges') caused the 10 northern tribes to revolt?
explanation: King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and listened to young men, fracturing the united kingdom into Judah and Israel.

question: Who was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, who erected golden calves at Bethel and Dan to prevent pilgrimages to Jerusalem?
explanation: Jeroboam I feared losing the loyalty of his people if they went to the Temple in Jerusalem, creating a persistent national snare.

question: Which king of Judah allied with wicked King Ahab through marriage and was rebuked by prophet Jehu: 'Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD?'
explanation: Godly King Jehoshaphat allied with Ahab by marriage (Jehoram married Athaliah), nearly dying in Ahab's disastrous battle at Ramoth Gilead.

question: Who was Elisha's greedy servant who ran after healed Naaman to demand silver and garments, and was cursed with Naaman's leprosy?
explanation: Elisha said to Gehazi: 'The leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and your descendants forever.' And he went out from his presence leprous, as white as snow.

question: What Syrian army officer smothered his sick king Ben-Hadad with a wet thick cloth to seize the Syrian throne, fulfilling Elisha's prophecy?
explanation: Hazael took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over King Ben-Hadad's face so that he died; and Hazael reigned in his place.

question: Who was the high priest who led the temple restoration when young King Joash collected funds from the people?
explanation: Joash did what was right all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him, making a chest for the collection at the temple gate.

question: What Assyrian field commander (rabshakeh) stood near the conduit of the upper pool and blasphemed the God of Israel in Hebrew to intimidate Jerusalem?
explanation: The Rabshakeh stood and called out with a loud voice in Hebrew, urging Jerusalem not to trust in Hezekiah or the LORD.

question: What king of Babylon was struck with clinical lycanthropy (madness), eating grass like oxen for seven seasons until he recognized the Most High God?
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar was driven from men and ate grass like oxen until his hair grew like eagles' feathers, after which he praised and honored the King of heaven.

question: Who was the last king of Babylon, the coregent who drank from the Jerusalem Temple's sacred vessels and was slain the night the city fell to the Medo-Persians?
explanation: That very night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was slain, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom.

question: What Persian governor of Samaria, along with Tobiah the Ammonite, relentlessly mocked and opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls?
explanation: Sanballat and Tobiah were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the well-being of the children of Israel and mocked: 'Even if a fox climbs on it, their stone wall will break down!'

question: Who was the royal grandson of King Jehoiachin who served as governor of Judah and led the first return of exiles to rebuild the Temple?
explanation: Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem.

question: What post-exilic prophet urged the returned exiles to consider their ways and prioritize rebuilding God's ruined temple over paneling their own homes?
explanation: Haggai asked: 'Is it time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, and this temple to lie in ruins? Consider your ways!'

question: Who was the herdsman and tender of sycamore fruit from Tekoa who was called by God to prophesy against the wealthy northern kingdom of Israel?
explanation: Amos answered Amaziah: 'I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet, but I was a sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit.'

question: What unfaithful wife did God command the prophet Hosea to love again, redeeming her from the slave market for 15 shekels of silver?
explanation: Hosea bought back his adulterous wife Gomer, demonstrating God's relentless redeeming covenant love for unfaithful Israel.

question: Who was the father of King David, a resident of Bethlehem who had eight sons?
explanation: Samuel was sent to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for God had chosen a king from among Jesse's sons, the youngest being David.

question: Who was David's eldest brother who sharply criticized young David for coming down to the battle against Goliath in the Valley of Elah?
explanation: Eliab's anger was aroused against David, and he said, 'Why did you come down here? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness?'

question: What Philistine king of Gath gave David and his men the border city of Ziklag while David was evading King Saul?
explanation: King Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath, gave David the town of Ziklag, which belonged to the kings of Judah thereafter.

question: Who was King Saul's loyal general who crowned Saul's son Ishbosheth king over northern Israel at Mahanaim after Saul's death?
explanation: Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ishbosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim, making him king over Israel.

question: What sister of Absalom was violated by her half-brother Amnon, inciting Absalom's vengeful murder of Amnon two years later?
explanation: Amnon wronged his half-sister Tamar; her full brother Absalom hated Amnon and arranged his assassination at a sheep-shearing feast.

question: Who was the wise woman of Tekoa hired by Joab to tell a fabricated parable to King David to convince him to bring banished Absalom home?
explanation: Joab put words in the mouth of a wise woman from Tekoa, who told a story about two fighting brothers to appeal to David's mercy.

question: What Cushite runner announced the tragic news of Absalom's death to King David, causing David to weep: 'O my son Absalom—my son, my son Absalom!'?
explanation: The Cushite delivered the message: 'May the enemies of my lord the king... be as that young man is!' David was deeply moved and wept bitterly.

question: Which of David's mighty men defended a plot of barley (lentils) alone against the Philistines when the people fled, working a great victory for the LORD?
options: Shammah son of Agee the Hararite
explanation: Shammah stationed himself in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines; so the LORD brought about a great victory.

question: Who was the Hittite soldier, one of David's thirty mighty men, whose murder David orchestrated after impregnating his wife Bathsheba?
explanation: David sent a letter by Uriah's own hand to Joab: 'Set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck down and die.'

question: What prophet confronted King Rehoboam and Judah with an army of 180,000 men, commanding them not to fight against their northern brethren?
explanation: The word of God came to Shemaiah: 'You shall not go up nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel. Return every man to his house.'

question: Which king of Israel reigned for only seven days before burning the royal citadel down upon himself when Omri besieged Tirzah?
explanation: Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah; when he saw the city was taken, he went into the citadel of the king's house and burned it over himself with fire.

question: What Phoenician king of Tyre supplied King Solomon with cedar and cypress timber from Lebanon and gold for the Temple building projects?
explanation: King Hiram of Tyre had always loved David and entered a formal trade treaty with Solomon to supply Lebanon timber in exchange for wheat and oil.

question: Who was the priest of Bethel who commanded prophet Amos to flee back to the land of Judah and eat bread there instead of prophesying against Jeroboam II?
explanation: Amaziah the priest of Bethel told Amos: 'Go, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah. There eat bread, and there prophesy. But never prophesy again at Bethel.'

question: Which post-exilic prophet urged the Jewish community not to despise 'the day of small things' as the Temple foundation was laid?
explanation: Zechariah asked: 'For who has despised the day of small things? For these seven rejoice to see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.'

question: Who was the chief officer of the Temple in Jeremiah 20 who struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate?
explanation: Pashhur struck Jeremiah and put him in stocks; Jeremiah prophesied his name would be Magor-Missabib ('Terror on every side').

question: Which king of Judah cut up Jeremiah's prophetic scroll with a penknife and threw the pieces into a brazier fire in his winter palace?
explanation: King Jehoiakim had three or four columns read, cut them with a scribe's knife, and cast them into the fire until the entire scroll was consumed.

question: Who was the Roman officer (centurion) at Capernaum whose servant was paralyzed and whom Jesus praised for remarkable faith?
explanation: The centurion recognized military authority and divine authority, stating: 'Lord, I am not worthy that You should come under my roof. But only speak a word.'

question: Who was the ruler of the Capernaum synagogue whose twelve-year-old daughter was raised from the dead by Jesus?
explanation: Jairus fell at Jesus' feet pleading for his dying daughter; Jesus told him, 'Do not be afraid; only believe,' and raised her to life.

question: Which woman out of whom Jesus had cast seven demons stood at the foot of the cross and was the first to see the risen Christ?
explanation: Mary Magdalene was delivered from seven demons and became the first apostle to the apostles, announcing: 'I have seen the Lord!'

question: Who was the prominent woman, wife of Chuza who was Herod's household manager, who supported Jesus' ministry out of her private means?
explanation: Joanna the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others provided for Jesus and His disciples from their substance.

question: What apostle, named Levi in Luke 5, left his lucrative tax booth in Capernaum to follow Jesus and hosted a great banquet for fellow tax collectors?
explanation: Levi left all, rose up, and followed Jesus, making Him a great feast in his own house with a large crowd of tax collectors.

question: Which of the twelve apostles was from Bethsaida, introduced Nathanael to Jesus, and calculated that 200 denarii of bread would not feed the 5,000?
explanation: Philip was tested by Jesus regarding how to buy bread for the multitude, calculating that two hundred denarii would not be sufficient.

question: Which apostle was the brother of Simon Peter, initially a disciple of John the Baptist, who brought Peter and the boy with five loaves to Jesus?
explanation: Andrew was always bringing people to Jesus: first his brother Simon Peter, then the boy with loaves and fish, and later Greek seekers.

question: Who was the cousin of Barnabas who accompanied Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey but departed early from Perga?
explanation: John Mark left the mission at Perga in Pamphylia and returned to Jerusalem, causing a later disagreement between Paul and Barnabas.

question: Which Greek convert was taken to Jerusalem by Paul without being compelled to be circumcised, proving Gentile Christian liberty?
explanation: Paul writes: 'Yet not even Titus who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised,' demonstrating freedom from ceremonial circumcision.

question: What companion of Paul was left in Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach strange doctrine and to oversee church leadership?
explanation: Paul urged Timothy to remain in Ephesus that he might charge certain persons not to teach other doctrine nor give heed to fables.

question: Who was the first polygamist recorded in Genesis, who killed a young man for wounding him and composed a boastful song to his wives Adah and Zillah?
explanation: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah, and boasted: 'I have killed a man for wounding me... If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.'

question: Who is named in Genesis 4:22 as the instructor of every craftsman in bronze and iron?
explanation: Zillah bore Tubal-Cain, an instructor of every craftsman in bronze and iron; his sister was Naamah.

question: Who is described in Genesis 10:8-9 as a 'mighty hunter before the LORD' whose kingdom began at Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh?
explanation: Cush begot Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth; he was a mighty hunter before the LORD, founding Babel.

question: In Genesis 10:25, which descendant of Shem was named because 'in his days the earth was divided'?
explanation: To Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg (meaning division), for in his days the earth was divided.

question: What wife did Abraham marry after the death of Sarah, with whom he had six sons including Midian and Medan?
explanation: Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Keturah; she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

question: What Canaanite prince violated Jacob's daughter Dinah, leading her brothers Simeon and Levi to massacre the males of his city?
explanation: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite saw Dinah and violated her, provoking Simeon and Levi's deceitful and violent vengeance.

question: Who was Judah's daughter-in-law who disguised herself as a veiled prostitute at Enaim to bear twins Perez and Zerah by Judah?
explanation: Tamar secured the family line through Judah after his sons Er and Onan died; Perez is an ancestor in Christ's genealogy (Matthew 1:3).

question: What Egyptian name was given to Joseph by Pharaoh when he appointed him prime minister of Egypt?
explanation: Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-Paneah (often translated 'Revealer of secrets' or 'God speaks and lives').

question: Who was Joseph's Egyptian wife, the daughter of Potipherah priest of On, who bore Manasseh and Ephraim?
explanation: Pharaoh gave Joseph as wife Asenath, the daughter of Potipherah priest of On, who bore him two sons before the famine came.

question: What two Hebrew midwives feared God and defied Pharaoh's royal decree to murder newborn Hebrew boys?
explanation: The midwives Shiphrah and Puah feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded, but saved the male children alive.

question: Who was Moses' and Aaron's mother, of the tribe of Levi, who married Amram?
explanation: Amram took for his wife Jochebed, his father's sister; and she bore him Aaron and Moses (and Miriam).

question: Who was Aaron's wife, of the royal tribe of Judah, the sister of Nahshon?
explanation: Aaron took to wife Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon; and she bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

question: What two oldest sons of Aaron offered 'profane (unauthorized) fire' before the LORD at Sinai and were consumed by fire from God?
explanation: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer and offered profane fire before the LORD, and fire came out from the LORD and devoured them.

question: Who was the craftsman of the tribe of Dan appointed alongside Bezalel to build the Tabernacle?
explanation: God appointed with Bezalel 'Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan,' an engraver and designer.

question: Who held up Moses' hands along with Aaron during the battle against the Amalekites at Rephidim?
explanation: Aaron and Hur supported Moses' hands, one on one side and the other on the other side, until sunset, securing victory over Amalek.

question: Who was the giant king of Bashan whose iron bedstead measured nine cubits long by four cubits wide?
explanation: Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the giants; his iron bedstead was in Rabbah of the Ammonites, nine cubits long.

question: Who was the king of the Amorites who refused to let Israel pass through his land and was defeated at Jahaz?
explanation: Sihon king of the Amorites gathered all his people together and fought against Israel, but Israel defeated him with the edge of the sword.

question: What judge of Israel killed 70 of his half-brothers upon one stone at Ophrah to declare himself king, but was killed when a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head at Thebez?
explanation: Abimelech murdered his brothers to become king in Shechem; at Thebez, a certain woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.

question: Who was the youngest son of Gideon who survived Abimelech's massacre and told the Parable of the Bramble from Mount Gerizim?
explanation: Jotham climbed Mount Gerizim and warned Shechem through the fable of the trees choosing the thorny bramble as king.

question: Who was the father of King Saul, a mighty man of power from the tribe of Benjamin?
explanation: There was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, a mighty man of power, the father of Saul.

question: Who was the king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared contrary to God's explicit command, whom the prophet Samuel 'hacked in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal'?
explanation: Saul spared Agag and the best of the livestock; Samuel declared 'As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless' and executed him.

question: Who was David's mighty nephew, the brother of Joab and Asahel, who went with David into Saul's camp at night and took Saul's spear and water jug?
explanation: Abishai went with David into the camp while Saul slept, offering to strike Saul with the spear, but David forbade him.

question: Who was David's nephew who was 'as fleet-footed as a wild gazelle', pursued Abner in battle, and was killed with the butt end of Abner's spear?
explanation: Asahel refused to turn aside from chasing Abner; Abner struck him in the stomach with the blunt end of his spear, killing him.

question: Who was King Saul's concubine who guarded the bodies of her two sons and five stepsons from scavengers on a rock at Gibeah after they were executed?
explanation: Rizpah took sackcloth, spread it for herself on the rock from harvest until rain poured, preventing birds and beasts from touching the corpses.

question: Who was David's general whom David appointed over the army to replace Joab after Absalom's rebellion, only for Joab to murder him at the great stone in Gibeon?
explanation: Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him and struck him in the stomach with his sword, dropping his intestines to the ground.

question: Who was the Gittite commander from Philistine territory who displayed absolute loyalty to David during Absalom's rebellion, saying 'In whatever place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also your servant will be'?
explanation: Ittai the foreigner pledged complete allegiance to David and commanded a third of David's forces in the battle against Absalom.

question: What Benjamite rebel blew a trumpet and led a rebellion against David immediately following Absalom's death, declaring 'We have no part in David'?
explanation: Sheba son of Bichri led northern Israel away from David until a wise woman in Abel Beth Maachah had his head thrown over the wall to Joab.

question: Who was the priest who took over the High Priesthood alone under King Solomon when Abiathar was banished to Anathoth?
explanation: Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest to fulfill God's word concerning the house of Eli at Shiloh, putting Zadok in his place.

question: Who was Solomon's taskmaster over the forced labor who was stoned to death by the northern tribes when Rehoboam sent him to negotiate?
explanation: King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of the revenue and forced labor; but all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died.

question: Which king of Judah removed his grandmother Maachah from being queen mother because she had made an obscene image for Asherah?
explanation: King Asa removed Maachah his grandmother from being queen mother because she had made an obscene image, and he crushed it and burned it by the Brook Kidron.

question: Who was the prophet from Judah who cried out against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel by name prophesying: 'O altar, altar! A child, Josiah by name, shall be born to the house of David'?
