options: The unnamed man of God from Judah
explanation: A man of God from Judah prophesied against the altar at Bethel, foretelling King Josiah by name 300 years before his birth.

question: What prophet of Judah rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of relying on the LORD, declaring 'The eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth'?
explanation: Hanani the seer confronted Asa; Asa was enraged with the seer and put him in prison.

question: Who was the Levite who, filled with the Spirit of the LORD, prophesied to King Jehoshaphat: 'Do not be afraid nor dismayed... for the battle is not yours, but God's'?
explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel in the midst of the assembly, telling Jehoshaphat: 'Stand still and see the salvation of the LORD with you.'

question: Which priest and son of Jehoiada was stoned to death in the court of the Temple by order of King Joash after rebuking the people for forsaking God?
explanation: Joash did not remember the kindness of Jehoiada and killed his son Zechariah, who cried as he died: 'The LORD look on it, and repay!'

question: Who was the king of Judah who, upon becoming strong, arrogantly entered the sanctuary to burn incense and was confronted by 80 valiant priests led by Azariah?
explanation: Azariah the priest went in after him with eighty valiant priests of the LORD and withstood King Uzziah until leprosy broke out on him.

question: What wicked king of Judah sacrificed his own children in the fire in the Valley of Hinnom, made an altar modeled after a pagan altar in Damascus, and closed the doors of the Temple?
explanation: King Ahaz gathered the articles of the house of God, cut them in pieces, shut up the doors of the house of the LORD, and made altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

question: Who was the chief of the Babylonian executioners (captain of the guard) who supervised the burning of Jerusalem and the deportation of its people in 586 BC?
explanation: Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, burned the house of the LORD and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

question: What king of Babylon released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison after 37 years of captivity, spoke kindly to him, and gave him a seat at his royal table?
explanation: In the year he began to reign, Evil-Merodach king of Babylon released Jehoiachin from prison and gave him a regular daily allowance for the rest of his life.

question: Who was the High Priest who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylon and rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings?
explanation: Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren the priests built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings as written in the Law of Moses.

question: Who was the High Priest who rebuilt the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem with his brethren during Nehemiah's reconstruction?
explanation: Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests and built the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and hung its doors.

question: What Persian queen was deposed by King Ahasuerus for refusing to appear at his royal banquet to show her beauty to the guests?
explanation: Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command; the king's counselors advised that she be deposed so that her royal position be given to another.

question: What was the name of Haman's wife who advised him to build a 50-cubit gallows to hang Mordecai on?
explanation: His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to Haman: 'Let a gallows be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning suggest to the king that Mordecai be hanged on it.'

question: Who was the young bystander in Job who waited until Job's three friends had finished speaking before rebuking them for condemning Job without an answer?
options: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite
explanation: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite waited to speak because they were older than he, but his wrath was aroused against Job's three friends because they found no answer.

question: What daughter of Herodias danced before Herod Antipas and his nobles and asked for the head of John the Baptist on a platter?
explanation: The daughter of Herodias (identified historically by Josephus as Salome) danced, pleased Herod, and demanded the head of John the Baptist on a platter.

question: Who was the Jewish wife of Roman Governor Felix, mentioned in Acts 24:24 when Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come?
explanation: Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning faith in Christ.

question: Who was the sister of King Herod Agrippa II who accompanied him to Caesarea to hear Paul's defense before Festus in Acts 25:23?
explanation: Agrippa and Bernice entered with great pomp and entered the auditorium with the commanders and prominent men of the city to hear Paul.

question: What Christian couple risked their own necks for Paul's life and hosted churches in their home in Corinth, Ephesus, and Rome?
explanation: Paul greets Priscilla and Aquila: 'my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.'

question: What Christian believer in Rome is identified by Paul in Romans 16:7 as his kinsman and fellow prisoner, who was 'of note among the apostles' and was in Christ before Paul?
explanation: 'Greet Andronicus and Junia, my countrymen and my fellow prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.'

question: In 2 Timothy 1:16-18, what faithful brother from Ephesus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chain, searching diligently for him in Rome?
explanation: Paul prays: 'The Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.'

question: Who is named in Colossians 4:17 with the solemn apostolic exhortation: 'Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it'?
explanation: Paul explicitly charges Archippus (also addressed in Philemon as 'our fellow soldier'): 'Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it.'

question: What is the first book of the Holy Bible?
explanation: Genesis is the opening book of the Bible, recounting the creation of the heavens and the earth.

question: What is the final book in the New Testament and the Christian Bible?
explanation: Revelation (the Apocalypse of John) is the 66th and concluding book of the Bible.

question: How many books are there in total in the Protestant canon of the Bible?
explanation: The Protestant Bible contains 66 books: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New Testament.

question: How many books are in the Old Testament?
explanation: The Protestant Old Testament consists of 39 books, starting with Genesis and ending with Malachi.

question: How many books are in the New Testament?
explanation: The New Testament consists of 27 books, starting with Matthew and ending with Revelation.

question: Which book of the Bible contains 150 songs and prayers?
explanation: The Book of Psalms is the Bible's hymnbook, consisting of 150 individual poetic psalms.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Gospels?
explanation: The four Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Acts is the historical narrative of the early church.

question: Which Old Testament book tells the story of the Israelites' departure from Egypt?
explanation: Exodus describes the departure (exodus) of the children of Israel out of Egyptian slavery under Moses.

question: What is the collective name for the first five books of the Bible attributed to Moses?
explanation: The first five books (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) are called the Pentateuch or the Torah (Law).

question: Which book tells the history of the early Christian church and the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost?
explanation: Acts, written by Luke, records the birth and missionary expansion of the early church.

question: Which Old Testament wisdom book is primarily attributed to King Solomon and focuses on short sayings for wise living?
explanation: Proverbs opens with 'The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel' and provides divine wisdom for everyday life.

question: Which book is named after a young Moabitess who showed loyalty to her mother-in-law Naomi?
explanation: The Book of Ruth tells of Ruth's devotion to Naomi and her marriage to Boaz, becoming an ancestor of King David and Jesus.

question: Which book features a Jewish woman who became queen of Persia and saved her people from extermination?
explanation: The Book of Esther recounts Queen Esther risking her life before King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) to foil Haman's plot.

question: Which is the last book of the Old Testament?
explanation: Malachi is the final book of the Old Testament in standard Protestant and Catholic arrangements.

question: Which book follows immediately after Deuteronomy in the Old Testament?
explanation: Joshua follows Deuteronomy, continuing Israel's narrative as they cross the Jordan into Canaan.

question: Which book follows immediately after the Book of Joshua?
explanation: Judges follows Joshua, describing the cycles of rebellion, oppression, cry, and deliverance under judge-leaders.

question: Which book follows the Book of Judges in the English Bible?
explanation: Ruth is placed after Judges because its story occurs 'in the days when the judges ruled' (Ruth 1:1).

question: What is the longest single chapter in the Bible?
explanation: Psalm 119 contains 176 verses, celebrating God's word in an 8-verse-per-letter acrostic format.

question: What is the shortest chapter in the entire Bible?
explanation: Psalm 117 has only two verses, praising the Lord for His lovingkindness and truth.

question: Which Gospel writer was known as a tax collector before Jesus called him?
explanation: Matthew (also called Levi) was sitting at the tax collector's booth when Jesus said, 'Follow Me.'

question: Which Gospel writer was described by Paul as 'the beloved physician'?
explanation: Paul calls Luke 'the beloved physician' in Colossians 4:14; Luke also authored Acts.

question: Which apostle wrote the greatest number of individual letters in the New Testament?
explanation: The Apostle Paul authored 13 (or 14 if Hebrews is included) epistles in the New Testament.

question: What is the first book of the New Testament?
explanation: The Gospel according to Matthew stands as the opening book of the New Testament.

question: Which book tells the story of a prophet swallowed by a great fish after fleeing God's command?
explanation: The Book of Jonah details Jonah running from God's mission to Nineveh and being swallowed by a large fish.

question: Which Old Testament book contains visions of dry bones coming to life and four living creatures?
explanation: The prophet Ezekiel witnessed visions of God's chariot-throne and the valley of dry bones restored to life.

question: Which book features Daniel in the lions' den and three Hebrews in the fiery furnace?
explanation: The Book of Daniel chronicles God's miraculous deliverance in Babylon during the exile.

question: Which book has the famous passage: 'To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under heaven'?
explanation: Ecclesiastes chapter 3 begins with the famous poem on times and seasons appointed by God.

question: Which book explores the intense suffering of a blameless man and why the righteous suffer?
explanation: The Book of Job examines the problem of innocent suffering through the trials and speeches of Job and his friends.

question: Which is the longest prophetic book by chapter count (66 chapters)?
explanation: Isaiah contains 66 chapters, often called a miniature Bible due to its division into judgment and comfort.

question: Which prophet is known as the 'weeping prophet' and also wrote the book of Lamentations?
explanation: Jeremiah wept over Jerusalem's impending destruction and penned Lamentations in grief after the fall.

question: Which New Testament book is a letter addressed to the church in Rome setting forth Christian doctrine?
explanation: Paul's Epistle to the Romans is his most systematic theological presentation of the gospel and justification by faith.

question: Which book is known as the 'love chapter' because of chapter 13?
explanation: 1 Corinthians 13 is commonly called the 'love chapter' ('Love is patient, love is kind...').

question: Which letter lists the 'fruit of the Spirit' in chapter 5?
explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

question: Which letter contains the famous armor of God passage in chapter 6?
explanation: Ephesians 6 urges believers to put on the whole armor of God to stand against the wiles of the devil.

question: Which letter is often called the 'epistle of joy' because of Paul's frequent rejoicing while in prison?
explanation: Philippians is renowned for its joyful tone despite Paul's imprisonment: 'Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice!'

question: Which book contains the 'hall of faith' recounting champions of faith in chapter 11?
explanation: Hebrews 11 is famed as the 'hall of faith,' highlighting Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and others.

question: Which book emphasizes that 'faith without works is dead'?
explanation: The Epistle of James strongly argues that genuine living faith will naturally manifest in righteous actions.

question: How many letters did Peter write that are in the New Testament canon?
explanation: Peter wrote two canonical epistles: 1 Peter and 2 Peter.

question: How many epistles bear the name of John in the New Testament?
explanation: The Apostle John wrote three short epistles: 1 John, 2 John, and 3 John (in addition to his Gospel and Revelation).

question: Which short one-chapter book comes immediately before Revelation?
explanation: The Epistle of Jude stands directly before Revelation as the 65th book of the Bible.

question: Which book describes Moses leading Israel through 40 years of wandering in the wilderness and taking a census?
explanation: Numbers is named in the Greek/English tradition for the censuses taken at Sinai and on the plains of Moab.

question: Which book consists primarily of Moses' farewell speeches and the giving of the 'Shema' (Deut 6:4)?
explanation: Deuteronomy ('second law') contains Moses' review of God's covenant with Israel before his death on Mount Nebo.

question: Which book details the priestly laws, sacrificial offerings, and festivals of ancient Israel?
explanation: Leviticus deals with the responsibilities of the Levites, purity laws, sacrifices, and holiness code.

question: Which Old Testament book records the rebuilding of Jerusalem's temple after the Babylonian exile?
explanation: The Book of Ezra details the return of the exiles under Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the second temple.

question: Which Old Testament book records the cupbearer who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's broken walls in 52 days?
explanation: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, returned to Jerusalem and rebuilt the defensive walls in just 52 days.

question: Which gospel begins with: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God'?
explanation: The Gospel of John opens with the majestic prologue identifying Jesus as the eternal Logos/Word.

question: Which gospel is the shortest of the four and frequently uses the Greek word 'immediately' (euthus)?
explanation: The Gospel of Mark is 16 chapters long, fast-paced, and frequently emphasizes Jesus' immediate actions.

question: Which book has the romantic celebration of marital love between a bride and her beloved king?
explanation: The Song of Solomon (also called Canticles or Song of Songs) is a poetic celebration of romantic love.

question: Which book tells the dramatic story of Elijah confronting 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel?
explanation: Elijah's contest on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal is recorded in 1 Kings 18.

question: Which book tells of Elisha asking for a 'double portion' of Elijah's spirit as Elijah was taken into heaven in a whirlwind?
explanation: The ascension of Elijah and succession of Elisha with a double portion is recounted in 2 Kings 2.

question: Which two books of the Bible do not explicitly mention the word 'God' or 'Lord' in their original Hebrew text?
explanation: Neither Esther nor Song of Solomon contains an explicit mention of the primary divine names YHWH or Elohim in Hebrew.

question: Which Old Testament book is the shortest in length, consisting of only 21 verses?
explanation: Obadiah is the shortest book in the Old Testament, consisting of a single chapter of 21 verses pronouncing judgment on Edom.

question: Which New Testament book is the shortest by total word count?
explanation: 3 John is the shortest book in the New Testament by Greek word count (roughly 219 Greek words), just slightly shorter than 2 John (245 words).

question: Which book contains an account of the prophet Hosea being commanded by God to marry an unfaithful woman named Gomer?
explanation: Hosea's marriage to Gomer served as a living illustration of God's covenant love toward unfaithful Israel.

question: In the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), what is the first book of the Ketuvim (Writings) section?
explanation: In the traditional Hebrew canon, the Ketuvim (Writings) section opens with the Book of Psalms.

question: In the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), what is the very last book?
explanation: In the traditional Hebrew arrangement, 1 & 2 Chronicles (Divrei HaYamim) are placed last, concluding with Cyrus's decree to rebuild the temple.

question: How many books make up the collection traditionally known as the 'Minor Prophets' (The Twelve)?
explanation: The Minor Prophets comprise 12 books from Hosea to Malachi, called 'minor' due to brevity, not lesser importance.

question: Which prophet was a herdsman and tender of sycamore figs from Tekoa called to preach to the northern kingdom?
explanation: Amos stated, 'I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet, but I was a sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit.'

question: Which prophetic book prophesied specifically that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah?
explanation: Micah 5:2 prophesied: 'Yet out of you shall come forth to Me the One to be Ruler in Israel, whose goings forth are from of old.'

question: Which letter did Paul write to a Christian master urging him to receive back his runaway slave as a beloved brother?
explanation: Paul wrote to Philemon asking him to forgive and welcome back the runaway slave Onesimus as a brother in Christ.

question: Which two letters were written by Paul to a young pastor overseeing the church in Ephesus?
explanation: Paul urged Timothy to remain at Ephesus to instruct church leaders and guard sound doctrine.

question: Which young co-worker was left on the island of Crete by Paul to set things in order and appoint elders in every city?
explanation: Paul wrote to Titus: 'For this reason I left you in Crete, that you should set in order the things that are lacking and appoint elders.'

question: Which prophet predicted a devastating plague of locusts as a picture of the coming 'Day of the Lord' and prophesied the outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh?
explanation: Joel described the locust devastation and prophesied: 'I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh' (quoted by Peter at Pentecost in Acts 2).

question: Which prophetic book focuses exclusively on the total overthrow and doom of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria?
explanation: While Jonah preached repentance to Nineveh, Nahum prophesied its final destruction a century later.

question: Which prophet questioned God about how He could use the wicked Chaldeans (Babylonians) to punish a less wicked nation, and heard: 'The just shall live by his faith'?
explanation: Habakkuk's dialogue with God contains the famous declaration: 'The just shall live by his faith' (Hab 2:4).

question: Which post-exilic prophet urged Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest to finish rebuilding the second temple with four short dated sermons?
explanation: Haggai confronted the returned exiles for living in paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins.

question: Which post-exilic prophet saw apocalyptic night visions including four horsemen, a flying scroll, and Joshua crowned as high priest?
explanation: Zechariah ministered alongside Haggai and recorded eight striking night visions concerning Israel's future.

question: Which New Testament letter contains no mention of the sender's name in the text itself and argues that Jesus is superior to angels, Moses, and the Levitical priesthood?
explanation: The author of Hebrews is anonymous within the text, and its central theme is the supremacy and finality of Jesus Christ.

question: Which book has five poetic funeral laments over the fall of Jerusalem, four of which are 22-verse Hebrew acrostics?
explanation: Lamentations contains five poems mourning the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC, featuring alphabetical acrostics.

question: Which book begins: 'The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem. Vanity of vanities, all is vanity'?
explanation: Ecclesiastes (Qoheleth) opens with the teacher reflecting on the apparent futility of life apart from God.

question: Both the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles are addressed to which individual?
explanation: Luke dedicated both his Gospel and the Book of Acts to 'most excellent Theophilus'.

question: Which Pauline letter is fiercely defensive of justification by faith apart from the works of the Mosaic Law, famously rebuking Peter's hypocrisy at Antioch?
explanation: In Galatians 2, Paul recounts confronting Cephas (Peter) publicly when he withdrew from eating with Gentiles.

question: Which letter focuses heavily on countering a heresy devaluing Christ's deity and sufficiency, declaring that 'in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily'?
explanation: Colossians counters syncretistic false teaching by magnifying Christ as the creator, reconciler, and fullness of God.

question: Which book ends with the tragic execution of King Saul and his sons on Mount Gilboa?
explanation: 1 Samuel concludes with Saul's defeat and death on Mount Gilboa; 2 Samuel begins with David learning of Saul's death.

question: Which book is almost entirely devoted to the reign of King David as king over all Israel?
explanation: 2 Samuel recounts the entirety of David's 40-year reign, from Hebron to Jerusalem, including the Davidic Covenant.

question: Which book records the building of Solomon's magnificent temple in Jerusalem in chapters 5 through 7?
explanation: 1 Kings details King Solomon's wisdom, wealth, and the construction and dedication of the First Temple.

question: Which book records the fall and exile of the northern kingdom of Israel to Assyria (ch. 17) and Judah to Babylon (ch. 25)?
explanation: 2 Kings records Israel's exile in 722 BC by Shalmaneser/Sargon and Judah's fall in 586 BC under Nebuchadnezzar.

question: Which Old Testament historical books open with genealogies tracing all the way from Adam to the post-exilic community?
explanation: 1 Chronicles begins with 'Adam, Seth, Enosh...' and spends nine chapters tracing priestly, royal, and tribal lineages.

question: Which letter provides detailed qualifications for overseers (bishops) and deacons in chapter 3?
explanation: 1 Timothy 3 gives extensive moral and spiritual qualifications for church overseers and deacons.

question: In which epistle does Paul give comforting teaching on the rapture and resurrection of deceased believers: 'The dead in Christ will rise first'?
explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4 assures believers that departed Christians will not miss the return of Christ.

question: In which epistle does Paul warn believers not to be deceived that the day of the Lord has already come, explaining that the 'man of sin' must be revealed first?
explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2 corrects confusion about the day of the Lord and explains the rebellion and lawless one.

question: Which epistle is considered Paul's last will and testament, written from a Roman dungeon shortly before his martyrdom?
explanation: Paul writes in 2 Timothy 4: 'I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.'

question: Which book quotes the apocryphal Book of Enoch ('Behold, the Lord comes with ten thousands of His saints') and mentions an archangel disputing over Moses' body?
explanation: Jude cites Michael disputing with the devil over Moses' body and quotes Enoch's prophecy regarding divine judgment.

question: Which book contains letters dictated by Jesus to the seven churches in Asia Minor in chapters 2 and 3?
explanation: Revelation chapters 2 and 3 contain specific letters to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.

question: Which Gospel contains the seven famous 'I AM' statements of Jesus (e.g., 'I am the bread of life', 'I am the true vine')?
explanation: The distinctive seven metaphorical 'I AM' proclamations appear only in the Gospel of John.

question: Which Gospel has no parables in the narrative style found in Matthew, Mark, and Luke?
explanation: John features extended discourses and allegories (like the Good Shepherd) rather than classic narrative story-parables.

question: Which book has the famous prophetic promise of a 'New Covenant' written on human hearts rather than stone tablets?
explanation: Jeremiah 31:31-34 foretells the New Covenant, where God puts His law within them and writes it on their hearts.

question: Which Old Testament book contains visions of four world empires represented by a colossal statue made of four metals?
explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a statue with head of gold, chest of silver, thighs of bronze, and legs of iron, interpreted by Daniel.

question: Which letter addresses the unruly misuse of spiritual gifts, order in public worship, and the Lord's Supper?
explanation: 1 Corinthians 11-14 provides Paul's instructions on the Lord's Table, spiritual gifts, tongues, prophecy, and worship order.

question: Which letter contains Paul's deeply personal defense of his apostolic authority and his 'thorn in the flesh'?
explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:7-9, Paul speaks of a thorn in the flesh given to keep him humble, where God said, 'My grace is sufficient for you.'

question: Which book contains the 'kenosis' hymn describing Christ emptying Himself and taking the form of a bondservant?
explanation: Philippians 2:5-11 is the famous Christological passage describing Jesus' voluntary humiliation and supreme exaltation.

question: Which Gospel writer was known in the early church as Peter's interpreter and wrote primarily for a Roman/Gentile audience?
explanation: Early church fathers such as Papias recorded that Mark recorded the preaching and eyewitness testimony of Simon Peter.

question: Which letter is addressed to 'the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad' and contains strong practical wisdom resembling Proverbs?
explanation: James wrote to Jewish believers scattered in the diaspora, offering practical, pithy exhortations on trials and Christian living.

question: Which letter warns believers against scoffing false teachers in the last days who deny the Second Coming by saying 'all things continue as they were'?
explanation: 2 Peter 3 confronts scoffers and affirms that with the Lord one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

question: Which letter was written to assure Christians of eternal life, stating: 'These things I have written to you... that you may know that you have eternal life'?
explanation: 1 John was written with tests of genuine fellowship and faith so believers may possess full assurance of eternal salvation.

question: Which short letter is addressed to the 'elect lady and her children', warning not to receive into their home anyone bringing false doctrine?
explanation: 2 John is addressed to the 'elect lady' and warns against showing hospitable endorsement to itinerant deceivers.

question: Which short letter commends Gaius for his hospitality but strongly denounces a domineering church leader named Diotrephes?
explanation: 3 John praises Gaius for receiving traveling teachers and rebukes Diotrephes who loves to put himself first.

question: Which Old Testament book tells of a prophet commissioned to marry a prostitute, whose children were named Jezreel, Lo-Ruhamah, and Lo-Ammi?
explanation: Hosea named his three children symbolic names reflecting Israel's coming judgment and God's broken heart.

question: Which major prophet has sections written in Aramaic (chapters 2:4 through 7:28) rather than Hebrew?
explanation: The imperial and gentile-focused portions of Daniel were composed in Biblical Aramaic, the lingua franca of the Neo-Babylonian and Persian empires.

question: Which book contains the verse: 'He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God'?
explanation: Micah 6:8 is one of the Old Testament's most celebrated summaries of genuine godliness.

question: In the Jewish tradition, the five books of the Megillot (Festal Scrolls) are Ruth, Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes, Lamentations, and which other book?
explanation: The five Megillot read during annual Jewish festivals are Song of Songs (Passover), Ruth (Shavuot), Lamentations (Tisha B'Av), Ecclesiastes (Sukkot), and Esther (Purim).

question: Which book in the New Testament contains the word 'antichrist' (antichristos)?
explanation: Surprisingly, the exact term 'antichrist' appears exclusively in the Epistles of John (1 John and 2 John), not once in Revelation or Paul's letters.

question: Which New Testament epistle is the only one explicitly addressed to a non-Jewish, Gentile friend residing in Asia Minor?
explanation: Paul's letter to Philemon was addressed directly to an individual householder in Colossae alongside Apphia and Archippus.

question: Which prophetic book contains the oracle against King Belshazzar regarding the mysterious handwriting on the wall: 'MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN'?
explanation: Daniel 5 describes the fateful feast where the fingers of a man's hand wrote judgment on the palace plaster.

question: Which book has the earliest known reference to a 70-year duration for Judah's captivity in Babylon?
explanation: Jeremiah prophesied that the land would serve the king of Babylon for 70 years, which Daniel later studied (Daniel 9:2).

question: Which book in the Septuagint and Hebrew tradition contains chapters 1-4 with 22 verses each and chapter 3 with exactly 66 verses (3 times 22)?
explanation: In Lamentations, chapters 1, 2, 4, and 5 each have 22 verses, while chapter 3 has 66 verses, mirroring the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

question: In which New Testament book is Jesus described as a priest forever 'according to the order of Melchizedek'?
explanation: Hebrews chapter 7 elaborates on Psalm 110:4, demonstrating that Christ's priesthood precedes and supersedes the Levitical line.

question: Which Old Testament book records the vision of the valley of dry bones and the battle of Gog and Magog?
explanation: Ezekiel 37 contains the valley of dry bones, and chapters 38-39 describe the apocalyptic invasion of Gog of Magog.

question: Which book contains the famous prophecy of the 'Seventy Weeks' pointing to the arrival and cutting off of the Anointed One?
explanation: Gabriel gave Daniel the vision of 70 weeks (heptads) decreed for Jerusalem to finish transgression and bring everlasting righteousness.

question: Which book contains a vivid description of the heavenly New Jerusalem coming down out of heaven with twelve foundations of precious gemstones?
explanation: Revelation 21 depicts the New Jerusalem with twelve gates of pearl and twelve foundations decorated with every kind of precious stone.

question: Which Minor Prophet contains an intense oracle against Edom for rejoicing over Judah's destruction and looting their brother's possessions?
explanation: Obadiah condemns Edom (descendants of Esau) for their arrogance and violence against their brother Jacob.

question: In which New Testament book does the author note that he used his own large handwriting to conclude his epistle?
explanation: Paul writes in Galatians 6:11: 'See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand!'

question: In which letter does Paul send greetings from Tertius, the scribe/amanuensis who wrote down the epistle as Paul dictated?
explanation: Romans 16:22 states: 'I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.'

question: Which Pauline epistle was written to a church Paul had never personally visited prior to writing the letter?
explanation: Paul tells the Colossians and Laodiceans: 'I want you to know what a great conflict I have for you and those in Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.'

question: Which book has the famous proverb: 'Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He shall direct your paths'?
explanation: This classic passage of trust and divine guidance is found in Proverbs 3:5-6.

question: Which book mentions the enigmatic figure 'Agur son of Jakeh' who utters numerical proverbs ('There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say Enough') in chapter 30?
explanation: Proverbs 30 contains the words and numerical observations of Agur, son of Jakeh.

question: Which book contains the poem describing the virtuous wife ('woman of valor') who is far more precious than rubies in chapter 31?
explanation: Proverbs 31:10-31 is an acrostic poem commending the noble wife, taught by King Lemuel's mother.

question: Which book in the Old Testament records King Hezekiah's miraculous healing and the sun's shadow moving backward ten degrees?
explanation: Both 2 Kings 20 and Isaiah 38 record Hezekiah's illness, the poultice of figs, and the miracle of the sundial.

question: Which prophetic book concludes with the promise that God will send Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord?
explanation: The Old Testament closes in Malachi 4:5-6 with the prophecy of Elijah's coming, fulfilled in John the Baptist.

question: Which Old Testament book contains the vision of the high priest Joshua standing before the angel of the Lord while Satan accuses him, after which his filthy garments are replaced with rich apparel?
explanation: Zechariah 3 presents Joshua the high priest cleansed from guilt, a vivid depiction of imputed righteousness.

question: Which book describes the king of Judah, Manasseh, being captured with hooks and led with bronze chains to Babylon, where he repented?
explanation: While 2 Kings focuses only on Manasseh's idolatry, 2 Chronicles 33 records his deep repentance in Babylon and restoration to Jerusalem.

question: Which epistle quotes Jesus saying a beatitude not recorded in any of the four Gospels: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive'?
explanation: In Acts 20:35, Paul bids farewell to the Ephesian elders, reminding them of the Lord Jesus' words: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'

question: Which New Testament book contains the earliest written account of the Lord's Supper instructions ('For I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you...')?
explanation: 1 Corinthians (written around AD 54-55) predates the written Gospels, preserving the earliest recorded text of the Words of Institution.

question: Which Old Testament book details the construction, dimensions, and furnishings of the Tabernacle in the wilderness?
explanation: Exodus devotes chapters 25-31 to the Tabernacle design and chapters 35-40 to its construction and divine filling by God's glory.

question: Which book contains a detailed description of two monstrous creatures, 'Behemoth' and 'Leviathan', illustrating God's sovereign power over creation?
explanation: God challenges Job in chapters 40-41 by pointing to the untamable majesty of Behemoth and the terrifying fire-breathing Leviathan.

question: Which Gospel contains the detailed narrative of the disciples on the Road to Emmaus whose hearts burned within them as Jesus opened the scriptures?
explanation: The walk to Emmaus with Cleopas and his companion is a masterpiece found exclusively in Luke 24.

question: Which Gospel features the famous farewell discourse of Jesus to His disciples spanning chapters 14 through 17?
explanation: The Upper Room discourse and the High Priestly Prayer (John 17) are found only in the Gospel of John.

question: Which New Testament letter contains warnings against 'the doctrine of Balaam' and 'the teaching of the Nicolaitans'?
explanation: In the letter to the church in Pergamum, Jesus condemns those holding the teachings of Balaam and the Nicolaitans.

question: In which Old Testament book is there a narrative of Balaam's talking donkey and Balaam's four unwilling blessings over Israel?
explanation: Numbers 22-24 recounts King Balak of Moab hiring Balaam, whose donkey spoke after seeing the angel of the Lord.

question: Which prophetic book contains the line: 'For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'?
explanation: Hosea 8:7 warns of the inevitable consequences of idolatry: 'For they sow the wind, and reap the whirlwind.'

question: Which book has the profound vision of God measuring the temple and water flowing out from under the threshold, becoming a river too deep to cross?
explanation: Ezekiel 47 describes the life-giving river flowing from the temple sanctuary out toward the Dead Sea.

question: Which book contains God's promise to restore 'the years that the swarming locust has eaten'?
explanation: Joel 2:25 offers divine restoration: 'I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten... My great army which I sent among you.'

question: Which epistle explicitly warns believers: 'Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers'?
explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:14 commands: 'Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers. For what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness?'

question: In which Old Testament book is there a detailed prophecy of the suffering Servant: 'He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities'?
explanation: Isaiah 52:13 - 53:12 contains the supreme Old Testament prophecy of the suffering, substitutionary death, and resurrection of Christ.

question: Which Old Testament book records the installation of the bronze serpent on a pole so that anyone bitten could look upon it and live?
explanation: Numbers 21 describes fiery serpents judging Israel, and Moses making a bronze serpent, referenced by Jesus in John 3:14.

question: Which New Testament book concludes with the warning: 'If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book'?
explanation: The final solemn warning against adding to or subtracting from the prophetic words closes the Book of Revelation.

question: Which book has the account of the sun and moon standing still at Gibeon during a miraculous military campaign?
explanation: Joshua 10 records: 'Sun, stand still over Gibeon; and Moon, in the Valley of Aijalon.' And the sun stood still about a whole day.

question: Which book contains the story of Ehud the left-handed judge who delivered Israel by assassinating Eglon, the fat king of Moab?
explanation: Judges 3 details Ehud hiding a double-edged dagger on his right thigh and striking King Eglon in his private roof chamber.

question: Which book contains Jotham's famous fable of the trees seeking a king and choosing the thorny bramble?
explanation: Jotham told this barbed allegory from Mount Gerizim after Abimelech murdered Gideon's seventy sons to seize power.

question: Which book describes the tragic story of Jephthah's vow before going to battle against the Ammonites?
explanation: Jephthah made a rash vow to sacrifice whatever first came out of his doors, which turned out to be his only daughter.

question: Which New Testament book is addressed to an elder named Gaius and praises Demetrius as having a good testimony from everyone?
explanation: In 3 John 12, John commends Demetrius, stating that he has a good testimony from all, and from the truth itself.

question: Which book records the dramatic story of a prophet buying a potter's earthen flask and smashing it in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom as a symbol of Jerusalem's ruin?
explanation: Jeremiah 19 describes the prophet shattering the clay flask before elders and priests to declare that God will break this city irreparably.

question: Which prophet lay on his left side for 390 days bearing the iniquity of Israel and on his right side for 40 days for Judah?
explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to act out numerous dramatic sign-prophecies, including lying bound on his sides.

question: Which book has the line: 'For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea'?
explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 delivers this triumphant vision of worldwide knowledge of God's glory in the midst of dark judgments.

question: Which epistle contains the instruction: 'Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil'?
explanation: James 5:14-15 gives church instructions for praying over the sick in faith and confession of sins.

question: Which book mentions Jesus preaching 'to the spirits in prison, who formerly were disobedient... in the days of Noah'?
explanation: 1 Peter 3:19-20 contains this famous and intriguing passage about Christ proclaiming victory to imprisoned spirits.

question: In which New Testament book does Paul explicitly mention being caught up to the 'third heaven' in Paradise fourteen years earlier?
explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12, Paul speaks of an experience being caught up into Paradise where he heard inexpressible words.

question: Which book ends with God showing compassion on the great city containing more than 120,000 people who cannot discern between their right hand and their left, and also much livestock?
explanation: Jonah 4:11 closes with God's poignant question contrasting Jonah's grief over a withered gourd with God's mercy on Nineveh.

question: Which Old Testament book records the high priest Hilkiah discovering the lost 'Book of the Law' in the temple during King Josiah's renovations?
explanation: The rediscovery of the Torah sparked young King Josiah's sweeping national covenant renewal and Passover celebration.

question: Which prophetic book concludes with the poetic declaration: 'Though the fig tree may not blossom, nor fruit be on the vines... yet I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation'?
explanation: Habakkuk 3 closes with one of the most sublime confessions of unflinching trust in God amidst utter earthly devastation.

question: What was Jesus' first recorded public miracle, performed at a wedding?
explanation: At the wedding in Cana of Galilee, Jesus turned six stone waterpots of water into choice wine.

question: With what food items did Jesus miraculously feed five thousand men besides women and children?
explanation: Jesus took a boy's five barley loaves and two small fish, gave thanks, and fed over five thousand people.

question: How many baskets of leftover fragments did the disciples gather after the feeding of the five thousand?
explanation: They picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces that remained after the multitude had eaten.

question: Who stepped out of the boat and briefly walked on the water toward Jesus before beginning to sink?
explanation: Peter stepped out on the water to come to Jesus, but seeing the wind boisterous, he grew afraid and began to sink.

question: Whom did Jesus raise from the dead after he had been in the tomb for four days in Bethany?
explanation: Jesus commanded, 'Lazarus, come forth!' and Lazarus came out bound in graveclothes after four days in the tomb.

question: What sea did God part through Moses' outstretched staff so the Israelites could cross on dry ground?
explanation: The Lord drove the Red Sea back by a strong east wind all night, dividing the waters so Israel walked through on dry land.

question: What miraculous food did God rain down from heaven every morning to feed Israel in the wilderness?
explanation: God provided manna, a fine, flake-like substance tasting like wafers made with honey, for 40 years.

question: What words did Jesus speak to calm a violent storm on the Sea of Galilee?
explanation: Jesus arose and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, 'Peace, be still!' And the wind ceased and there was a great calm.

question: How long had a woman suffered from an issue of blood before touching the hem of Jesus' garment and being healed?
explanation: She had bled for twelve years and spent all her money on physicians without cure until touching Jesus' robe in faith.

question: What did Moses strike with his staff at Horeb to miraculously produce water for the thirsty Israelites?
explanation: God said: 'Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it.'

question: Whose daughter did Jesus raise from the dead, saying 'Talitha, cumi' ('Little girl, arise')?
explanation: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, begged Jesus to heal his daughter, and Jesus brought her back from death.

question: How many lepers did Jesus cleanse near the border of Samaria and Galilee, of whom only one returned to give thanks?
explanation: Jesus cleansed ten lepers, but only one—a Samaritan—turned back glorifying God and falling at His feet.

question: What blind beggar cried out repeatedly, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' outside Jericho and received his sight?
explanation: Blind Bartimaeus threw aside his cloak and cried out until Jesus called him and restored his sight.

question: How did four friends bring a paralyzed man to Jesus when the house in Capernaum was overflowing with crowds?
explanation: They uncovered the roof where Jesus was, broke through the tiles, and let down the bed on which the paralytic lay.

question: What fell down flat when the Israelites marched around it for seven days and shouted at the blast of trumpets?
explanation: When the priests blew the trumpets and the people gave a great shout, the walls of Jericho fell down flat.

question: What weapon or tool made of iron did the prophet Elisha cause to float on the water of the Jordan River?
explanation: When a man dropped an axe head into the water, Elisha threw in a stick, and the iron floated to the top.

question: How many times was the Syrian commander Naaman told to dip himself in the Jordan River to be healed of leprosy?
explanation: Elisha instructed Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times, after which his flesh was restored like that of a little child.

question: What animal spoke with a human voice to forbid a prophet's madness when an angel with a drawn sword blocked the road?
explanation: God opened the mouth of Balaam's donkey, who asked why Balaam had struck her three times.

question: What miracle consumed Elijah's water-soaked altar, sacrifice, wood, and stones on Mount Carmel?
options: Fire from the Lord out of heaven
explanation: The fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering, wood, stones, dust, and licked up the water in the trench.

question: Who was thrown into a den of hungry lions but emerged without a scratch because God sent an angel to shut their mouths?
explanation: Daniel told King Darius: 'My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, so that they have not hurt me.'

question: Who walked unharmed through a superheated fiery furnace accompanied by a fourth figure resembling the 'Son of God'?
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire without hurt, the fourth looking like the Son of God.

question: What tree did Jesus curse because it had leaves but no fruit, causing it to wither away to its roots immediately?
explanation: Seeing a leafy fig tree with no fruit, Jesus said, 'Let no fruit grow on you ever again,' and it immediately withered away.

question: What came out of the mouth of the first fish Peter caught on Jesus' instructions to pay the temple tax?
explanation: Jesus told Peter to throw out a hook, open the mouth of the first fish, and find a stater (coin) for both their taxes.

question: What did Jesus touch to instantly heal Peter's mother-in-law when she was lying sick with a high fever?
explanation: Jesus touched her hand, the fever left her, and she arose and served them.

question: Where did Jesus tell a blind man to go wash after anointing his eyes with mud made from saliva?
explanation: Jesus spat on the ground, made mud, anointed the man's eyes, and told him: 'Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam.' He went, washed, and came back seeing.

question: How long had the disabled man at the Pool of Bethesda been invalid before Jesus commanded him, 'Rise, take up your bed and walk'?
explanation: A certain man had an infirmity thirty-eight years; Jesus healed him on the Sabbath.

question: Into what herd of animals did Jesus send a legion of demons who had possessed a violent man living in the tombs?
explanation: The demons begged to enter a herd of about two thousand pigs, which ran violently down the steep place into the sea and drowned.

question: Whose severed right ear was healed when Jesus touched it during His arrest in the Garden of Gethsemane?
explanation: Peter cut off Malchus's ear with a sword, but Jesus touched his ear and miraculously healed him.

question: Whose mother was given a miraculous child in her extreme old age after laughing at God's promise?
explanation: Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son, Isaac, in his old age when Abraham was 100 and Sarah was 90.

question: What happened to the Egyptian army when they pursued the Israelites into the midst of the parted Red Sea?
options: The waters collapsed and drowned them all
explanation: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, the waters returned to their full depth, and not so much as one of Pharaoh's army remained.

question: What happened to the bronze serpent when people bitten by venomous snakes looked upon it?
explanation: Moses made a bronze serpent and put it on a pole; and if a serpent had bitten anyone, when he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

question: What happened to the waters of the Jordan River when the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant stepped into the brim?
options: The waters rose up in a heap upstream, leaving dry ground
explanation: As soon as the feet of the priests touched the edge of the water, the Jordan stopped flowing and piled up in a heap far away at Adam.

question: Whose dead son was raised to life after the prophet Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times?
explanation: Elijah cried out to the Lord and stretched himself upon the widow of Zarephath's son three times, and his life returned.

question: Whose dead son was raised to life after Elisha lay on him, mouth to mouth and eyes to eyes, until the child sneezed seven times?
explanation: Elisha prayed and lay upon the Shunammite's child until the boy became warm, sneezed seven times, and opened his eyes.

question: What happened to the jar of flour and jug of oil belonging to the widow of Zarephath during the severe drought?
options: They did not run out until the day the Lord sent rain
explanation: The bin of flour was not used up, nor did the jar of oil run dry, according to the word of the Lord spoken by Elijah.

question: What did Jesus do for a widow in the town of Nain who was on her way to bury her only son?
options: Touched the open coffin and raised the young man back to life
Sent His apostles to comfort her
explanation: Jesus said, 'Young man, I say to you, arise.' He who was dead sat up and began to speak, and Jesus presented him to his mother.

question: What happened when the disciples let down their nets at Jesus' command after fishing all night without catching anything in Luke 5?
options: They caught such a great number of fish that their nets began to break
They caught an old chest of gold
explanation: When they let down the nets, they caught so many fish that both boats were filled to the point of sinking.

question: What physical defect was healed on a Sabbath when Jesus told a man in the synagogue: 'Stretch out your hand'?
explanation: Jesus told the man with the withered hand to stretch it out, and it was completely restored as healthy as the other.

question: What happened when Peter and John commanded a man lame from birth at the Beautiful Gate: 'In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk'?
options: His feet and ankle bones immediately received strength and he walked and leaped
He fell back into the dust
He asked for silver and gold
explanation: Peter took him by the right hand and lifted him up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength; he leaped and praised God.

question: How did the Apostle Peter escape from Herod Agrippa's maximum-security prison on the night before his planned trial?
options: An angel struck his side, his chains fell off, and the iron gate opened on its own
His friends tunneled under the floor
explanation: An angel illuminated the cell, broke Peter's chains, and led him past guards and through the self-opening iron city gate.

question: What happened when Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns in a Philippian jail at midnight?
options: A great earthquake shook the foundations, doors opened, and everyone's chains were unfastened
The magistrates arrived with an apology
explanation: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, the prison doors flew open, and every prisoner's chains were loosened.

question: What did a poisonous viper do to Paul when it fastened onto his hand as he gathered firewood on the island of Malta?
options: Paul shook it off into the fire and suffered no harm
Paul had to cut off his hand
explanation: Paul shook off the beast into the fire and suffered no ill effects, causing the islanders to believe he was a god.

question: Whom did Peter raise from the dead in Joppa, a disciple renowned for her good deeds and charitable making of coats?
explanation: Peter knelt down and prayed, saying 'Tabitha, arise,' and she opened her eyes and sat up.

question: Who fell asleep and plummeted out of a third-story window during Paul's marathon midnight preaching in Troas, and was revived by Paul?
explanation: Young Eutychus sank into deep sleep, fell from the third story, and was taken up dead; Paul embraced him and his life was restored.

question: What miraculous sign happened to Aaron's rod among the twelve rods placed before the testimony in the Tabernacle?
options: It sprouted buds, blossoms, and ripe almonds overnight
It became a bronze serpent permanently
explanation: Aaron's rod for the house of Levi sprouted, produced buds, blossomed, and yielded ripe almonds, confirming his priestly calling.

question: What happened to the bitter waters of Marah so that the thirsty Israelites could drink them?
options: Moses cast a specific tree shown to him by the Lord into the water, and it became sweet
Moses struck the water with his staff
explanation: Moses cried out to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree. When he cast it into the waters, the waters were made sweet.

question: What did God provide when the Israelites complained bitterly about eating only manna in the wilderness?
options: A wind bringing dense clouds of quail from the sea
explanation: A wind from the Lord brought quail from the sea and blew them all around the camp about two cubits deep.

question: How did Jesus heal a Roman centurion's paralyzed and suffering servant without ever stepping into the man's house?
options: By speaking the word of healing from a distance due to the centurion's great faith
By writing a prayer on a parchment
By having Peter visit the house
explanation: The centurion said, 'Only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.' Jesus marveled at his faith and the servant was healed that very hour.

question: What happened to a woman who had been bent double for 18 years and could not straighten herself up at all?
options: Jesus laid His hands on her on the Sabbath, and immediately she was made straight and glorified God
She made an offering at the altar
explanation: Jesus called her and said, 'Woman, you are loosed from your infirmity,' laid His hands on her, and she immediately stood upright.

question: What supreme miracle is the bedrock of the Christian faith, where Jesus conquered death on the third day?
explanation: The resurrection of Jesus Christ on the third day is the cornerstone of Christian faith and apostolic preaching.

question: How many stone waterpots did Jesus command to be filled with water before it turned to wine at Cana?
explanation: There were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of purification of the Jews, containing twenty or thirty gallons each.

question: In the feeding of the four thousand recorded in Matthew 15 and Mark 8, how many loaves and fish did Jesus start with?
options: Seven loaves and a few small fish
explanation: In the feeding of the 4,000, they had seven loaves and a few little fish, yielding seven large baskets of leftovers.

question: How many large baskets (spuris) of fragments remained after Jesus fed the four thousand?
explanation: They took up seven large hampers or baskets (spuris) full of broken pieces left over.

question: In the miraculous catch of fish after the resurrection in John 21, exactly how many large fish were counted in the unbroken net?
explanation: Simon Peter went up and dragged the net to land, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three; and yet the net was not broken.

question: What was the name of the high priest's servant whose right ear Peter cut off with a sword and Jesus healed?
explanation: The Apostle John specifically records the servant's name as Malchus.

question: Which of the ten plagues in Egypt was the first one that Pharaoh's magicians could NOT duplicate, confessing 'This is the finger of God'?
explanation: When Aaron struck the dust of the earth and it became lice, the magicians tried with their secret arts but failed, saying 'This is the finger of God.'

question: What was the tenth and most catastrophic plague inflicted upon Egypt before Pharaoh let Israel go?
explanation: At midnight the Lord struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon.

question: How did the prophet Elisha heal the bad, bitter water of the spring of Jericho that was causing barrenness and death?
options: He threw salt from a new bowl into the spring
He threw a stick into it
He built a stone altar over it
explanation: Elisha said, 'Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it.' He threw salt into the spring, and the water was healed of death and barrenness.

question: What did Elisha instruct a poor widow in debt to borrow from her neighbors to miraculously fill with oil and save her sons from slavery?
explanation: Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels from everywhere, not just a few; her one jar of oil kept pouring until every borrowed vessel was full.

question: How did Elisha neutralize a poisonous stew made with wild gourds for the sons of the prophets at Gilgal?
options: He poured wine into the pot
He cast meal (flour) into the pot
He cast salt into the pot
explanation: When they cried 'There is death in the pot,' Elisha said, 'Then bring flour,' cast it into the pot, and the stew was safe to eat.

question: With how many barley loaves did Elisha feed one hundred men of God, with food left over according to the word of the Lord?
explanation: A man from Baal Shalisha brought 20 loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain, which fed 100 men with leftovers remaining.

question: What miracle occurred when a deceased man's body was hastily thrown into the tomb of the prophet Elisha?
options: The tomb lit up with fire
As soon as the dead man touched Elisha's bones, he revived and stood on his feet
The dead man's relatives heard singing
explanation: When the dead body touched the bones of Elisha, the man revived and stood up on his feet.

question: What miraculous sign was given to King Hezekiah through the prophet Isaiah to confirm that God would add 15 years to his life?
options: The shadow on the sundial of Ahaz moved backward ten degrees
Water sprang out of the temple pavement
explanation: The Lord brought the shadow ten degrees backward on the sundial of Ahaz as a sign of Hezekiah's recovery.

question: During Joshua's battle against the Amorite kings at Gibeon, what two celestial bodies stood still at his prayer?
options: The sun and the morning star
explanation: The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and the moon stopped until the nation had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

question: What fell from heaven during Joshua's battle at Beth-horon that killed more enemy soldiers than the swords of the Israelites?
explanation: The Lord cast down large hailstones from heaven on them as far as Azekah, and more died from the hailstones than from the sword.

question: What double miracle with a fleece of wool confirmed to Gideon that God would save Israel by his hand?
options: Fleece wet while ground dry, then fleece dry while ground wet
Fleece turned white, then turned black
Fleece caught fire, then turned to gold
explanation: First night dew was on the fleece only and dry ground; second night it was dry on the fleece only and dew on all the ground.

question: What happened to the Philistine god Dagon when the captured Ark of the Covenant was placed in his temple at Ashdod?
options: Dagon fell facedown twice before the ark, and his head and hands were broken off
explanation: Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the Ark; the second morning his head and both hands were severed on the threshold.

question: What unusual method did Jesus use to heal a blind man at Bethsaida whose vision was restored in two stages (first seeing men like trees walking)?
options: Spit on his eyes and laid His hands on him
Commanded him to fast for three days
explanation: Jesus spat on his eyes and put His hands on him; the man first saw men walking like trees, then Jesus touched him again and he saw clearly.

question: In what region did Jesus cast out the demonic spirit called 'Legion'?
explanation: Jesus arrived in the country of the Gerasenes (or Gadarenes), opposite Galilee, where the demoniac came out from the tombs.

question: How did Jesus heal a man who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech in the region of the Decapolis?
options: Rebuked him from across the road
Put His fingers into his ears, spat, touched his tongue, and said 'Ephphatha'
Anointed his neck with olive oil
Had the disciples lay hands on him
explanation: Jesus put His fingers into his ears, spat, touched his tongue, looked up to heaven, sighed, and said 'Ephphatha' ('Be opened').

question: In the miracle of Jesus raising Lazarus, how many sisters did Lazarus have, who greeted Jesus outside Bethany?
explanation: Mary and Martha were Lazarus's sisters who sent word to Jesus and spoke with Him before Lazarus was raised.

question: Which Roman official had a servant who was paralyzed and dreadfully tormented, prompting Jesus to marvel at his faith?
explanation: A Roman centurion (commander of 100 soldiers) displayed faith greater than any Jesus had found even in Israel.

question: What physical signs occurred at the exact moment Jesus died on the cross at Golgotha?
options: The sun began to rain fire
The temple veil tore in two, the earth quaked, rocks split, and tombs were opened
Hail and brimstone fell on Herod's palace
The sea rolled back five miles
explanation: The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom; the earth shook, the rocks were split, and graves opened.

question: On the day of Pentecost in Acts 2, what miraculous sound and visual phenomena filled the house where the apostles were gathered?
options: A thunderous trumpet and white light
A rushing mighty wind and divided tongues like fire resting on each of them
A river of water and singing angels
explanation: Suddenly a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind filled the house, and divided tongues as of fire sat upon each of them.

question: What extraordinary medical phenomenon occurred through the Apostle Peter in the streets of Jerusalem in Acts 5?
options: People drank water from his cup
People carried the sick so that at least his passing shadow might fall on some of them and heal them
explanation: They brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at least Peter's shadow passing by might overshadow some, and they were all healed.

question: What items touched to Paul's skin were carried to the sick so that diseases left them and evil spirits went out in Ephesus?
explanation: God worked unusual miracles through Paul: handkerchiefs or aprons brought from his body healed illnesses and expelled demons.

question: What sorcerer was struck temporarily blind by the Apostle Paul on the island of Cyprus for opposing the proconsul Sergius Paulus?
explanation: Paul confronted Elymas the sorcerer, and immediately a dark mist fell on him, and he went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

question: What happened to the Egyptian sorcerers' staffs when Aaron threw down his rod before Pharaoh and it became a serpent?
options: Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods
explanation: The magicians threw down their rods and they also became serpents, but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

question: How did God demonstrate His call to Moses at Mount Horeb with Moses' own hand?
options: His hand held holy fire without burning
His hand became leprous as snow when put into his cloak, and was restored when put back
explanation: Moses put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, it was leprous as snow; when he put it back, it was restored like his other flesh.

question: What was the very first plague inflicted upon the land of Egypt through Moses and Aaron?
explanation: Aaron lifted up his rod and struck the waters of the Nile, and all the waters turned to blood, killing the fish.

question: Which plague in Egypt was accompanied by continuous thunder, hail, and fire running along the ground?
explanation: The seventh plague was massive hail mixed with fire, unprecedented in severity in all the history of Egypt.

question: For how many days did thick darkness cover the land of Egypt during the ninth plague while the Israelites had light in their dwellings?
explanation: Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days, but Israel had light.

question: What happened to the rebel Korah, Dathan, and Abiram when they challenged Moses' leadership in Numbers 16?
options: The ground split open beneath them and swallowed them and their households alive into Sheol
A pillar of cloud consumed them
explanation: The ground split open, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with their households and all their goods.

question: Whose hand withered instantly when he pointed it to order the arrest of a man of God at the altar in Bethel?
explanation: King Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar saying 'Seize him!' and his hand withered so that he could not pull it back, until the prophet prayed for him.

question: What miraculous judgment fell upon Gehazi, Elisha's servant, after he greedily pursued Naaman for silver and garments?
options: Naaman's leprosy clung to him and his descendants forever
He lost the ability to walk
explanation: Elisha declared: 'The leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and your descendants forever.' And Gehazi went out leprous, white as snow.

question: When the Syrian army surrounded Dothan to capture Elisha, what did Elisha pray for his fearful servant Gehazi to see?
options: A swarm of hornets attacking Syria
The mountain full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha
An angelic archangel with a shield
explanation: The Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

question: What did Elisha pray would happen to the Syrian raiding troops who came down against him at Dothan?
options: That God strike them with blindness
That their chariot wheels fall off
That an earthquake swallow their horses
explanation: God struck them with blindness at Elisha's word; Elisha then led them straight into the capital of Samaria before opening their eyes.

question: What miracle happened to Samson in Judges 15 after he slaughtered a thousand Philistines with a fresh donkey's jawbone and was dying of thirst?
options: Rain poured only on his head
God split the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water gushed out for him to drink
A spring opened in the jawbone itself
explanation: God split the hollow basin at Lehi, and water came out, and when Samson drank, his spirit returned and he revived (En Hakkore).

question: What miracle occurred when the prophet Elijah struck the waters of the Jordan River with his rolled-up mantle?
options: The waters parted to the right and left so Elijah and Elisha crossed on dry land
explanation: Elijah took his mantle, rolled it up, and struck the water; it divided this way and that, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

question: What did Elisha do immediately after Elijah was taken to heaven, using Elijah's fallen mantle at the Jordan?
options: Struck the Jordan water, crying 'Where is the Lord God of Elijah?', and the water parted again
explanation: Elisha picked up Elijah's mantle, struck the water, and the Jordan divided again so he could cross.

question: What happened when Jesus was in the synagogue at Capernaum on a Sabbath and a man possessed by an unclean spirit cried out in Luke 4?
options: Jesus rebuked the demon, saying 'Be quiet, and come out of him!' and it came out without hurting him
explanation: Jesus commanded the unclean demon to come out, which threw the man into the midst and came out of him without injuring him.

question: What miracle did Jesus perform for an official at Capernaum whose son was close to death twenty miles away in Cana?
options: He gave the father a vial of oil
He told him 'Go your way; your son lives,' and the fever left at that exact hour
He rode a donkey to Capernaum immediately
He sent Peter and John to pray
explanation: The father confirmed that at the seventh hour yesterday—the precise moment Jesus said 'Your son lives'—the fever broke.

question: In John 6, when Jesus' disciples were rowing across the Sea of Galilee about three or four miles in the middle of a dark storm, what terrifying sight did they see?
options: Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat
A lightning bolt hitting their mast
explanation: They saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat, and they were afraid, but He said: 'It is I; do not be afraid.'

question: When the disciples were unable to cast out a demon from an epileptic boy in Mark 9, what did Jesus tell them about why they had failed?
options: 'This kind can come out by nothing but prayer and fasting'
explanation: Jesus explained to His disciples in private: 'This kind can come out by nothing but prayer and fasting.'

question: What miraculous judgment befell King Herod Agrippa I in Acts 12 when he gave an oration and accepted the people's cry, 'The voice of a god and not of a man!'?
options: An angel of the Lord struck him, and he was eaten by worms and died
He went mad and lived with wild oxen
His throne collapsed into a sinkhole
explanation: Because he did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him, and he was eaten by worms and died.

question: What happened to the evangelist Philip immediately after he baptized the Ethiopian eunuch on the desert road to Gaza?
options: He rode the chariot to Ethiopia
The Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and he was found at Azotus
He returned on foot to Jerusalem
He lived in the desert for forty days
explanation: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more; Philip was found at Azotus.

question: In Acts 14, what miracle did Paul perform at Lystra that caused the local pagan citizens to think Barnabas was Zeus and Paul was Hermes?
options: He commanded a man crippled from his mother's womb to stand upright on his feet, and he leaped and walked
He called fire down on their altar
explanation: Paul told the lifelong crippled man, 'Stand upright on your feet!' And he leaped and walked, prompting the crowds to declare gods had come down in human likeness.

question: Whom did the Apostle Paul heal of fever and dysentery on the island of Malta following the shipwreck?
explanation: The father of Publius lay sick with fever and dysentery. Paul entered in, prayed, laid his hands on him, and healed him.

question: What sudden judgment struck Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5 when they lied to the Holy Spirit about the sale price of their property?
options: They each fell down dead at Peter's feet and were carried out for burial
explanation: Hearing Peter's words, Ananias fell down and breathed his last; about three hours later, Sapphira entered, lied, and also fell dead.

question: How did Jesus heal a man who had been born completely blind in John 9, which astonished the Pharisees?
options: He pronounced a blessing over his head
He spat on the ground, made clay with the saliva, anointed the man's eyes, and sent him to wash in Siloam
He washed his eyes in the Jordan
He touched his eyes with an olive branch
explanation: Jesus made clay of spittle, spread it on the blind man's eyes, told him to wash in Siloam, and the man came back seeing.

question: Which of the four Gospels is the ONLY one to record the miracle of Jesus raising Lazarus from the dead?
explanation: The raising of Lazarus after four days in Bethany is recorded uniquely in the Gospel of John.

question: Which Gospel is the ONLY one to record the miraculous catch of 153 large fish after Jesus' resurrection?
explanation: The post-resurrection miraculous draught of 153 fish on the Sea of Tiberias is exclusive to John 21.

question: Which Gospel is the ONLY one to record the miracle of the coin found in the fish's mouth to pay the temple tax?
explanation: Only Matthew (a former tax collector) records the miraculous stater found in the fish's mouth for the temple shekel.

question: Which Gospel is the ONLY one to record the raising of the widow of Nain's son from the bier?
explanation: The resurrection of the widow's son at Nain is found exclusively in Luke 7.

question: Which miracle is the ONLY public miracle performed by Jesus recorded in all four canonical Gospels before His resurrection?
explanation: The feeding of the five thousand is the only pre-resurrection miracle recounted in all four Gospels.

question: In the miracle of Jesus healing the blind man at Bethsaida in two stages (Mark 8:24), what exact words did the man say after Jesus' first touch?
explanation: He looked up and said: 'I see men like trees, walking.' Then Jesus put His hands on his eyes again and he was fully restored.

question: What Greek word translated 'Ephphatha' did Jesus utter with a deep sigh when healing the deaf and mute man in the Decapolis?
explanation: Mark records the Aramaic word 'Ephphatha', which he translates for his readers as 'that is, Be opened.'

question: What Greek word translated 'Talitha, cumi' did Jesus utter when raising Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter?
options: 'Little girl, I say to you, arise'
explanation: Jesus took her by the hand and said, 'Talitha, cumi,' which is translated, 'Little girl, I say to you, arise.'

question: In 2 Kings 3, what miracle did Elisha announce for the allied armies of Israel, Judah, and Edom dying of thirst in the wilderness of Edom?
options: Rain fell out of a blue sky
Dry valley trenches filled with water without wind or rain, and the red morning light deceived Moab into thinking it was blood
A spring opened in the rock of Petra
explanation: Elisha said: 'Make this valley full of ditches... you shall not see wind, nor rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water.' The morning sun on the water appeared red as blood to the Moabites.

question: In 1 Kings 18, how many barrels (pots) of water did Elijah command to be poured over his offering and wood on Mount Carmel before praying?
options: 12 barrels in total (4 barrels poured 3 times)
explanation: Elijah said, 'Fill four waterpots with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice and on the wood.' He commanded them to do it a second and third time (12 pots total).

question: What did the prophet Isaiah instruct King Hezekiah's attendants to apply to Hezekiah's lethal boil to bring about his physical recovery?
explanation: Isaiah said, 'Take a lump of figs.' So they took and laid it on the boil, and Hezekiah recovered.

question: In Numbers 12, who was struck with snow-white leprosy for seven days after speaking against Moses because of his Cushite wife?
explanation: When the cloud departed from above the Tabernacle, Miriam became leprous, as white as snow; Moses cried out for her healing, and she was shut out of the camp 7 days.

question: What miracle confirmed Gideon's reduced army of 300 men when he spied on the Midianite camp at night?
options: Overhearing a Midianite tell his friend a dream about a loaf of barley bread tumbling into the camp and overturning a tent
A sudden bolt of lightning striking the tent
A spring springing up at his feet
explanation: Gideon overheard a Midianite describe a cake of barley bread tumbling into the Midianite camp, overturning their tent, symbolizing Gideon's victory.

question: In Exodus 32, what did Moses do to the Golden Calf that Israel had forged while he was on Mount Sinai?
options: Burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it
Set it up as a warning monument
explanation: Moses took the calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the children of Israel drink it.

question: What miracle happened to King Uzziah (Azariah) of Judah when he arrogantly entered the temple sanctuary to burn incense before the Lord?
options: Leprosy broke out on his forehead right before the eighty priests, and he remained a leper until death
explanation: While Uzziah was furious with the priests holding the censer, leprosy erupted on his forehead; he was hurried out and dwelt in an isolated house.

question: In John 2, how many firkins or gallons did each of the six stone waterpots at Cana hold according to the text?
options: Two or three firkins (measures) each (about 20-30 gallons each)
explanation: The six stone waterpots contained 'two or three firkins apiece' (Greek metretes), totaling roughly 120-180 gallons of water transformed into wine.

question: In Luke 1, what miracle occurred to the elderly priest Zacharias when he doubted the angel Gabriel's prophecy that Elizabeth would bear a son?
options: He became paralyzed in his legs
He was struck mute (unable to speak) until the day his son John was named
His hair turned white as snow
explanation: Gabriel struck Zacharias mute for his disbelief until he wrote on a tablet 'His name is John', at which point his tongue was loosed.
