question: In Acts 3, at which gate of the Jerusalem temple was the 40-year-old congenital lame man healed by Peter and John?
explanation: He was laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of those who entered.

question: In Acts 9, who was the paralyzed man in Lydda bedridden for eight years whom Peter commanded: 'Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you. Arise and make your bed'?
explanation: Peter found a certain man named Aeneas who had been bedridden eight years and was paralyzed, and he arose immediately.

question: In Acts 16, what spirit possessed the slave girl in Philippi whom Paul cast out, infuriating her masters who lost their profit?
options: A spirit of divination (spirit of Python / Pythian spirit)
explanation: Luke writes she was possessed by 'a spirit of divination' (Greek pneuma pythona), who cried out that Paul and Silas proclaimed the way of salvation.

question: In Acts 19, what happened to the seven sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva when they tried to cast out a demon using Jesus' name without faith?
options: The man with the evil spirit leaped on them, overpowered them, and they fled naked and wounded
explanation: The evil spirit replied: 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?' Then the man leaped on them and overpowered them.

question: In 1 Kings 13, what happened to the pagan altar at Bethel when the unnamed man of God prophesied against it?
options: The altar split apart and the ashes poured out from it, exactly as prophesied
A serpent came out of the stones
explanation: The altar was split apart and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given.

question: When the disobedient prophet from Judah in 1 Kings 13 was killed by a lion on his return journey, what miraculous behavior did the lion and donkey exhibit?
options: The lion devoured both the prophet and the donkey
The lion did not eat the body nor tear the donkey, and both stood peacefully beside the corpse
The lion carried the corpse back to Bethel
The donkey kicked the lion to death
explanation: Passersby saw the corpse thrown in the road, with the lion and donkey standing beside the corpse: the lion had not eaten the carcass nor mauled the donkey.

question: What miracle happened to King Jeroboam's sick son Abijah when Jeroboam's disguised wife went to consult the blind prophet Ahijah at Shiloh?
options: He was instantly healed upon her return
Ahijah recognized her before she entered, and prophesied the child would die the moment her feet entered the city gate
The child became king for one year
The child was struck with blindness
explanation: The moment Jeroboam's wife stepped across the threshold of the house in Tirzah, the child died, exactly as Ahijah foretold.

question: What celestial or meteorological miracle occurred when the prophet Samuel called upon the Lord during the wheat harvest in 1 Samuel 12?
options: A solar eclipse darkened the sun
Thunder and rain poured down during the dry summer wheat harvest season
explanation: Samuel called upon the Lord, and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day (an unheard-of event during the dry summer harvest), and all the people greatly feared.

question: What miracle occurred when the Philistines returned the Ark on a cart pulled by two milk cows that had never been yoked and had their calves shut up at home?
options: The cows ran back to their calves
The cows went straight along the road toward Beth-Shemesh lowing as they went, turning neither right nor left
explanation: The cows took the straight highway toward Beth-Shemesh without being driven, confirming the plagues were from God.

question: What happened to seventy men of Beth-Shemesh when they irreverently looked inside the holy Ark of the Covenant?
options: The Lord struck them down and they died
explanation: God struck the men of Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the Ark of the Lord; He struck fifty thousand and seventy men (or 70 men of the leaders).

question: What happened to Uzzah when he put out his hand to steady the Ark of God when the oxen stumbled on the threshing floor of Nachon?
options: God's anger burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there for his error and he died beside the Ark
explanation: Uzzah touched the sacred Ark contrary to the Law, and God struck him dead there by the Ark of God (Perez Uzzah).

question: In John 5, what angelological or traditional belief was associated with the Pool of Bethesda that drew the blind, lame, and paralyzed?
options: An angel went down at a certain season into the pool and stirred up the water; whoever stepped in first was healed
The water flowed directly from Eden
A golden coin lay at the bottom
explanation: The sick waited for the moving of the water, believing that an angel stirred the pool and the first person into the water was healed.

question: In the miracle of Jesus raising Lazarus, what reason did Martha give when Jesus said, 'Take away the stone'?
options: 'Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days'
explanation: Martha said, 'Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days' (KJV: 'he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days').

question: Which of the following was a unique miraculous detail about the clothing of the Israelites throughout their forty years in the Sinai wilderness?
options: Their clothes turned bright white like snow
Their clothes did not wear out on them nor did their feet swell
Their clothes changed color with the seasons
explanation: Moses reminded Israel: 'Your garments did not wear out on you, nor did your foot swell these forty years.'

question: What miracle in 2 Kings 19 occurred overnight when King Sennacherib of Assyria besieged Jerusalem and blasphemed the God of Israel?
options: A massive flood drowned the Assyrian cavalry
The angel of the Lord went out and killed 185,000 soldiers in the camp of the Assyrians
Fire rained from heaven on their tents
explanation: That night the angel of the Lord struck 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians, and when men arose early the next morning, there were corpses all around.

question: What happened to two companies of fifty soldiers and their captains sent by King Ahaziah to seize Elijah on top of a hill?
options: They were blinded by bright light
Fire came down from heaven and consumed both captains and their fifty men
They were swallowed by the earth
explanation: Elijah answered: 'If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.' And fire fell and burned them up.

question: What did the third captain sent by King Ahaziah do differently that spared him and his fifty men from celestial fire?
options: He brought a peace offering of silver
He fell on his knees before Elijah and pleaded for his life and the lives of his men
He sent a message through a dove
explanation: The third captain bowed before Elijah and begged: 'O man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.'

question: In Matthew 8, in what town did Jesus heal Peter's mother-in-law and many others who were sick and possessed at sunset?
explanation: Jesus entered Capernaum, came into Peter's house, and healed his mother-in-law of her fever.

question: In Matthew 15, what was the nationality or background of the desperate mother whose daughter was severely demon-possessed, whose persistent faith Jesus commended?
explanation: She was a woman of Canaan (a Greek, a Syro-Phoenician by birth in Mark) from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

question: What happened when Jesus walked past a man blind from birth and His disciples asked: 'Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?'
options: Jesus said the man had sinned in a previous life
Jesus answered: 'Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but that the works of God should be revealed in him'
explanation: Jesus clarified that his congenital blindness was not divine retaliation for specific family sin, but an occasion for God's glory.

question: In Mark 11, on what day of Passion Week did Jesus' disciples observe that the cursed fig tree had withered completely down to its roots?
options: The next morning as they passed by
explanation: In the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots, and Peter called Jesus' attention to it.

question: In Luke 22, during Jesus' intense agony in the Garden of Gethsemane, what miraculous or rare physical manifestation took place as He prayed?
options: A pillar of cloud descended over Him
His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground
His hair turned white as snow
explanation: Being in agony, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground (hematidrosis).

question: In Matthew 27, what extraordinary resurrection miracle accompanied Christ's death and resurrection?
options: The bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised, came out of graves, and appeared to many in Jerusalem
Elijah and Moses returned to the temple
King David's tomb opened and spoke
explanation: Many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised, and coming out of the graves after His resurrection, entered the holy city and appeared to many.

question: In Acts 9, on the road to Damascus, what miraculous event transformed Saul the persecutor of Christians?
options: An earthquake knocked his horse down
A light from heaven brighter than the sun shone around him, and Jesus spoke to him: 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
An angel handed him two stone tablets
He was struck mute for forty days
explanation: A light shone from heaven, Saul fell to the earth, was struck blind for three days, and heard the voice of the risen Lord Jesus.

question: Whom did the Lord send to lay hands on Saul in Damascus so that something like scales fell from his eyes and he regained his sight?
explanation: A disciple at Damascus named Ananias went to the street called Straight and laid hands on Saul, restoring his sight and baptizing him.

question: In Acts 10, what miraculous vision appeared three times to the Apostle Peter on a rooftop in Joppa around the sixth hour?
options: A great sheet knit at the four corners let down from heaven containing all kinds of four-footed animals and creeping things
explanation: Peter saw heaven opened and an object like a great sheet descending, with God saying: 'What God has cleansed you must not call common.'

question: In Acts 14, after Paul was stoned in Lystra and dragged outside the city presumed dead, what miracle occurred as the disciples stood gathered around him?
options: He was buried in a nearby tomb
He rose up, walked back into the city, and departed the next day for Derbe
An angel carried him through the air to Antioch
He remained in a coma for two weeks
explanation: Though stoned and left for dead outside the city, as the disciples gathered around him, Paul stood up and went into the city.

question: In Acts 27, during the catastrophic two-week storm at sea, what miraculous revelation did an angel give to Paul regarding the 276 souls on board?
options: Ten people would perish in the waves
There would be no loss of life among them, but only of the ship
The ship would land safely in Rome without shipwreck
explanation: Paul told the crew: 'There will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship... God has granted you all those who sail with you.'

question: What miraculous judgment occurred when Korah's 250 followers offered incense with their bronze censers before the Tabernacle?
options: They were swallowed by an earthquake
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men offering incense
The censers melted onto their hands
explanation: While the earth swallowed Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, a separate fire from the Lord consumed the 250 men offering incense.

question: What was done with the 250 bronze censers of the men consumed by fire in Numbers 16 as a perpetual warning to Israel?
options: They were cast into the Dead Sea
They were beaten into hammered plates as a covering for the bronze altar
They were buried outside the camp
They were kept inside the Ark
explanation: Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers and had them hammered out into sheets to overlay the altar as a memorial.

question: In Joshua 7, how was the secret thief Achan discovered when the camp was consecrated following Israel's defeat at Ai?
options: A prophet named him in a dream
God directed the lot progressively by tribe (Judah), by clan (Zerahites), by family (Zabdi), and man by man until Achan was taken
An angel pointed to his tent
explanation: The Lord miraculously revealed the guilty party through the sacred lot: Judah, Zerahite clan, Zabdi family, and finally Achan son of Carmi.

question: What physical miracle occurred when Jonathan and his armor-bearer attacked the Philistine garrison at Michmash in 1 Samuel 14?
options: The sun stood still for five hours
A supernatural earthquake struck and the earth quaked, causing very great trembling and confusion in the Philistine camp
explanation: There was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the earth shook, so that it was a very great trembling from God.

question: In Daniel 5, during Belshazzar's sacrilegious feast using gold vessels from Jerusalem's temple, what miraculous hand appeared and terrified the king?
options: A hand carrying a fiery sword
The fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall opposite the lampstand
A hand holding a balance scale
A hand striking the banquet table in half
explanation: In the same hour the fingers of a man's hand appeared and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace.

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who stopped to help the wounded traveler beaten by robbers on the road to Jericho?
explanation: Both a priest and a Levite passed by on the other side, but a Samaritan had compassion, bound his wounds, and took care of him.

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what did the younger son feed when he ran out of money during a severe famine?
explanation: He hired himself out to a citizen of that country who sent him into the fields to feed swine, longing to fill his stomach with their carob pods.

question: What did the loving father do when he saw his returning prodigal son while he was still a long way off?
options: Ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him
explanation: When he was still a great way off, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.

question: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave in the wilderness to find the one that was lost?
explanation: Jesus asked: 'What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one which is lost?'

question: In the Parable of the Lost Coin, how many silver coins did the woman originally possess before losing one?
explanation: The woman had ten silver drachmas; when she lost one, she lit a lamp, swept the house, and searched carefully until she found it.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, which seed sprang up quickly but withered away under the scorching sun because it had no deep root?
explanation: Some fell on stony places where they did not have much earth; when the sun was up they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered away.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what happened to the seeds that fell along the wayside (by the road)?
options: The birds came and devoured them
They were washed away by a flood
explanation: As he sowed, some seed fell by the wayside; and the birds came and devoured them.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what choked the growing plants that sprang up among the thorns?
options: Cares of this world and deceitfulness of riches
explanation: Jesus explained that seed among thorns represents hearing the word, but the cares of this world and deceitfulness of riches choke the word.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what yields did the seed on good ground produce?
options: Thirty, sixty, and a hundred fold
explanation: Seed falling on good ground yielded a crop: some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

question: In the Parable of the Wise and Foolish Builders, where did the wise man build his house?
explanation: Jesus compared anyone who hears His words and does them to a wise man who built his house on the rock.

question: What happened to the house built on the sand when the rain descended, floods came, and winds blew?
options: It fell, and great was its fall
It suffered only minor roof damage
explanation: The rain fell, the floods came, the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell, and great was its fall.

question: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, how many virgins were wise and how many were foolish?
explanation: Five of them were wise, and five were foolish.

question: What essential supply did the five foolish virgins neglect to take with them in their vessels?
explanation: Those who were foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them, but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

question: At what time of night was the sudden cry made: 'Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him!'?
explanation: At midnight a cry was heard: 'Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him!'

question: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, what is notable about the mustard seed compared to other garden seeds?
options: It is the brightest in color
It is the smallest of all seeds, yet grows into a large tree where birds can nest
explanation: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which indeed is the least of all seeds, but when it is grown becomes a tree so birds nest in its branches.

question: In the Parable of the Pearl of Great Price, what did the merchant do when he found one pearl of extraordinary value?
options: Sold all that he had and bought it
Bargained the seller down to half price
explanation: When he had found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.

question: In the Parable of the Hidden Treasure, what did a man do when he found a treasure hidden in a field?
options: For joy he hid it, sold all that he had, and bought that field
explanation: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and for joy over it he sells all he has and buys that field.

question: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector (Publican), what was the tax collector's humble prayer?
options: 'God, I thank You that I am not like other men'
'God, be merciful to me a sinner!'
'Blessed are You, King of the universe'
explanation: The tax collector beat his breast, saying: 'God, be merciful to me a sinner!'

question: In the Parable of the Rich Fool, what did the rich man plan to do after producing an overwhelming bumper harvest?
options: Tear down his barns and build bigger ones to store his wealth, saying 'Eat, drink, and be merry'
Donate his field to the temple
explanation: He said: 'I will pull down my barns and build greater... Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; take your ease; eat, drink, and be merry.'

question: What did God say to the rich fool in Luke 12 that very night?
options: 'Fool! This night your soul will be required of you'
explanation: God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul will be required of you; then whose will those things be which you have provided?'

question: In the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares (Weeds), who sowed the bad tares into the farmer's wheat field?
explanation: While men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way. The master said, 'An enemy has done this.'

question: When the servants asked if they should pull up the tares immediately, what did the master tell them to do?
options: Let both grow together until the harvest, lest they uproot the wheat with them
explanation: He said, 'No, lest while you gather up the tares you also uproot the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest.'

question: In the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25, how many talents did the master distribute to his three servants?
options: Five to one, two to another, and one to another
explanation: To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability.

question: What did the servant who received one talent do with his master's money?
options: Went and dug in the earth and hid his lord's money
explanation: He who had received one talent went and dug in the ground, and hid his lord's money out of fear.

question: In the Parable of the Unmerciful Servant, after the king forgave the servant an immense debt of 10,000 talents, what did that servant do to a fellow servant who owed him just 100 denarii?
options: Laid hands on him, choked him, and had him thrown into prison until he paid
explanation: He grabbed his fellow servant by the throat, demanded payment, showed no mercy, and cast him into debtor's prison.

question: In the Parable of the Two Sons in Matthew 21, what did the first son say when told to go work in the vineyard, and what did he actually do?
options: Said 'I will not,' but afterward regretted it and went
Said 'I will go, sir,' but did not go
Said nothing and slept all day
explanation: He answered and said, 'I will not,' but afterward he regretted it and went.

question: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, what was the beggar Lazarus's condition on earth?
options: A wealthy merchant who lost everything
Full of sores, laid at the rich man's gate, desiring crumbs from the table
explanation: A certain beggar named Lazarus was laid at his gate, full of sores, desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table.

question: Where was Lazarus carried by angels when he died?
explanation: The beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom; the rich man also died and was buried, lifting up his eyes in torment.

question: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, what did the tormented rich man beg Abraham to send Lazarus to do?
options: Dip the tip of his finger in water and cool his tongue, for he was tormented in flame
explanation: He cried: 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.'

question: In the Parable of the Persistent Widow in Luke 18, to whom did the widow continually appeal for justice?
options: An unjust judge who did not fear God nor regard man
explanation: There was in a certain city a judge who did not fear God nor regard man, whom the widow persistently petitioned: 'Get justice for me from my adversary.'

question: Why did the unjust judge finally grant the persistent widow her legal justice?
options: Because her continual coming wearied and bothered him
Because she gave him a large bribe
explanation: He thought: 'Because this widow troubles me I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.'

question: In the Parable of the Friend at Midnight, how many loaves of bread did the host ask to borrow to feed his unexpected visitor?
explanation: He went to his friend at midnight and said: 'Friend, lend me three loaves; for a friend of mine has come to me on his journey, and I have nothing to set before him.'

question: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard, what wage did the vineyard owner agree to pay the early morning workers?
explanation: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

question: What wage did the laborers hired at the eleventh hour receive at the end of the day in Matthew 20?
options: One denarius (the exact same full day's wage)
explanation: When those hired about the eleventh hour came, each received a denarius, demonstrating God's sovereign grace and generosity.

question: In the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers (Tenants), what did the wicked tenants do to the landowner's son when he sent him?
options: Cast him out of the vineyard and killed him to seize his inheritance
explanation: They said, 'This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance.' So they took him and cast him out of the vineyard and killed him.

question: In the Parable of the Wedding Banquet in Matthew 22, what happened to a guest who was found not wearing a wedding garment?
options: He was given a new robe
He was bound hand and foot and cast into outer darkness
He was asked to pay a fine
He was seated at the lowest table
explanation: The king commanded his servants: 'Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'

question: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats in Matthew 25, on which side does the King place the righteous sheep?
explanation: He will set the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left.

question: In the Sheep and Goats discourse, what does the King say to those on His right hand?
options: 'Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world'
explanation: The King will say: 'Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.'

question: In the Parable of the Leaven, a woman hid leaven in how many measures of meal until it was all leavened?
explanation: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal till it was all leavened.

question: In the Parable of the Dragnet in Matthew 13, what did the fishermen do with the good and bad fish when the net was drawn to shore?
options: Threw all back into the lake
Gathered the good into vessels, but threw the bad away
Fed the bad fish to birds
explanation: When the net was full, they drew it to shore, sat down, gathered the good into vessels, but threw the bad away, depicting the final judgment.

question: In the Parable of the Barren Fig Tree in Luke 13, for how many years had the owner come seeking fruit on the fig tree without finding any?
explanation: He said to the keeper of his vineyard, 'Look, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down; why does it use up the ground?'

question: What did the vinedresser ask the owner to allow for the barren fig tree before cutting it down?
options: To let it alone this year also, until he digs around it and fertilizes it
To graft an olive branch into it
To cut off only the top branch
explanation: The vinedresser answered: 'Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it. And if it bears fruit, well. But if not, after that you can cut it down.'

question: When invited to a wedding feast, what place does Jesus advise guests to take to avoid public humiliation?
options: The place of honor at the head
explanation: When you are invited, go and sit down in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes he may say, 'Friend, go up higher.'

question: What universal spiritual principle does Jesus emphasize after discussing wedding feast seating in Luke 14?
options: 'For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted'
'Wisdom is justified by all her children'
'Give and it will be given to you'
explanation: Jesus declared: 'For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.'

question: In the Parable of the Two Debtors told to Simon the Pharisee in Luke 7, one debtor owed 500 denarii and the other 50. When the creditor forgave both, who will love him more?
options: The one to whom he forgave more (five hundred)
explanation: Simon correctly answered: 'I suppose the one whom he forgave more.' Jesus said to him, 'You have rightly judged.'

question: In Nathan's famous parable confronting King David about his sin with Bathsheba, what did the rich man take from the poor man?
options: His one little ewe lamb that grew up with his children
explanation: The poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb, but the rich man spared his own flocks and took the poor man's lamb to dress for his guest.

question: What dramatic words did Nathan the prophet speak to King David after David angrily declared the selfish rich man deserved to die?
explanation: Nathan looked King David in the face and said, 'You are the man!' exposing his adultery with Bathsheba and murder of Uriah.

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what three honor gifts did the father order for the returned younger son before killing the fatted calf?
options: A crown, a horse, and a sword
The best robe, a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet
A bag of gold, a staff, and an ox
A harp, a new coat, and a shield
explanation: The father said to his servants: 'Bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.'

question: How did the elder brother react when he came in from the field and heard music, dancing, and learned of the celebration for the prodigal?
options: He was angry and refused to go in
He packed his bags to leave
explanation: The older brother was angry and would not go in; therefore his father came out and pleaded with him.

question: Why did Jesus often speak to the crowds in parables according to Matthew 13?
options: To reveal spiritual mysteries to seekers while concealing them from hardened hearts
To speak in riddles for poetry
explanation: Jesus explained: 'Because it has been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.'

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, what two substances did the Samaritan pour into the wounded traveler's cuts and injuries?
explanation: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil (to soothe) and wine (to disinfect/cleanse).

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, how much money did the Samaritan leave with the innkeeper to care for the wounded man?
explanation: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and promised to repay whatever more was spent.

question: In Luke 10, what specific question prompted Jesus to tell the Parable of the Good Samaritan?
options: 'How can a man be born again?'
'Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar?'
'What must I do to inherit the earth?'
explanation: A lawyer, seeking to justify himself, asked Jesus: 'And who is my neighbor?' leading Jesus to tell the parable.

question: In the Parable of the Unjust (Shrewd) Steward in Luke 16, what did the steward do when he knew he was about to be fired for wasting his master's goods?
options: Stole the remaining silver and fled to Egypt
Called his master's debtors and reduced their bills so they would welcome him into their homes
Pleaded for mercy on his knees
explanation: He shrewdly discounted the promissory notes of those owing oil and wheat so they would be indebted to him after his dismissal.

question: In the Parable of the Unjust Steward, why did the master commend the dishonest steward in Luke 16:8?
options: Because he repented of his theft
Because he had dealt shrewdly / prudently
Because he gave half to charity
explanation: The master commended the unjust manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the sons of this world are more shrewd in their generation than the sons of light.

question: In the Parable of the Minas in Luke 19, how many servants did the nobleman call, and how much money did he give to each?
options: Three servants, each given different amounts
Ten servants, each given one mina
Twelve servants, each given five minas
Five servants, each given ten talents
explanation: He called ten of his servants, delivered to them ten minas, and said to them: 'Do business till I come.'

question: In the Parable of the Minas, what reward did the first servant receive whose mina had produced ten minas more?
explanation: The master said, 'Well done, good servant; because you were faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities.'

question: In the Parable of the Great Banquet in Luke 14, which of the following was NOT one of the excuses given by the invited guests?
options: 'I have bought a piece of ground, and I must go and see it'
'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them'
'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come'
explanation: The three specific excuses in the banquet parable were: inspecting purchased land, testing five yoke of oxen, and having married a wife.

question: When the original guests rejected the invitation to the Great Banquet in Luke 14, where did the master send his servant to find guests?
options: Into the streets and lanes, and into the highways and hedges to compel them to come in
explanation: He brought in the poor, crippled, blind, and lame from the streets, and compelled travelers in highways and hedges to fill his house.

question: In the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25, how many talents did the second servant earn on his initial two talents?
explanation: He who had received two talents came and said, 'Lord, you delivered to me two talents; look, I have gained two more talents besides them.'

question: In Matthew 25, what was done with the one talent taken away from the lazy and fearful servant?
options: Given to the servant who had ten talents
Kept in the master's private vault
explanation: The master ordered: 'Therefore take the talent from him, and give it to him who has ten talents.'

question: In the Parable of the Growing Seed found ONLY in Mark 4:26-29, how does the seed sprout and grow?
options: By continuous human intervention day and night
The earth produces crops by itself (automatically): first the blade, then the head, after that the full grain
explanation: The earth yields crops by itself (Greek automate): first the blade, then the head, after that the full grain in the head, while the sower sleeps and rises.

question: In Jotham's fable in Judges 9, which tree was the ONLY one willing to accept the offer to rule over the trees?
explanation: The olive, fig, and vine refused to abandon their fruitfulness to sway over trees, but the worthless bramble welcomed kingship.

question: In Isaiah 5, the 'Song of the Vineyard' describes a well-tended vineyard planted on a fruitful hill that disappointed its owner by producing what?
explanation: He expected it to bring forth good grapes, but it brought forth wild grapes (be'ushim, sour/foul fruit), representing rebellious Israel.

question: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant in Matthew 18, what was the astronomical size of the servant's forgiven debt?
explanation: One was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents—an unpayable debt representing millions of days' wages.

question: In Matthew 18, what prompted Jesus to tell the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant?
options: Peter asking how often he should forgive his brother, suggesting up to seven times
The Pharisees accusing disciples of Sabbath breaking
explanation: Peter asked if forgiving seven times was sufficient; Jesus replied, 'I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.'

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the 'seed' specifically represent according to Jesus' own interpretation in Luke 8:11?
explanation: Jesus clearly explains: 'Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.'

question: In the interpretation of the Parable of the Sower, who immediately snatches away the word from the hearts of those along the wayside?
explanation: The devil comes and takes away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.

question: In the Parable of the Wheat and Tares, what do the 'tares' (weeds/darnel) represent according to Jesus in Matthew 13:38?
options: The sons of the wicked one
explanation: Jesus explained: 'The good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the wicked one.'

question: In the Parable of the Wheat and Tares, who are the reapers at the end of the age?
explanation: Jesus stated: 'The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are the angels.'

question: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, what did Abraham tell the rich man when he pleaded for Lazarus to warn his five surviving brothers?
options: 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them'
explanation: Abraham said to him, 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.'

question: What piercing conclusion did Abraham deliver when the rich man argued that if one rose from the dead, his brothers would repent?
options: 'If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead'
'Lazarus is too weak to walk back'
explanation: Abraham answered: 'If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead.'

question: In Luke 17, Jesus told a short parable about a servant coming in from plowing or tending sheep. What does the master expect him to do first?
options: Gird himself and serve the master supper first, and afterward eat and drink
explanation: The master says, 'Prepare something for my supper, and gird yourself and serve me till I have eaten and drunk, and afterward you will eat and drink.'

question: What confession does Jesus teach disciples to say after doing all things commanded of them in Luke 17:10?
options: 'We have earned great merit before God'
'We are unprofitable servants. We have done what was our duty to do'
explanation: Jesus said: 'So likewise you, when you have done all those things which you are commanded, say, We are unprofitable servants. We have done what was our duty to do.'

question: In the Parable of the Faithful and Wise Steward in Luke 12, what distinguishes the faithful servant?
options: He spends the master's money on charity
He gives the household their portion of food in due season
He stays awake for seven days straight
He leads a rebellion against harsh overseers
explanation: The faithful and wise steward is made ruler over his master's household to give them their portion of food in due season.

question: In Luke 12, what judgment falls on the servant who knew his master's will, yet did not prepare himself or do according to his will?
options: He shall be beaten with few stripes
He shall be beaten with many stripes
He will be demoted one rank
He will be given a second chance
explanation: That servant who knew his master's will, and did not prepare himself or do according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.

question: In Luke 14, Jesus gives two practical parables on the 'Cost of Discipleship'. What are they?
options: Building a tower and a king going to war
Buying a field and weaving a garment
Planting a vineyard and building an ark
explanation: Jesus asks who intends to build a tower without counting the cost to finish it, or what king goes to war without considering if his 10,000 can face 20,000.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the rocky/stony soil represent in spiritual life?
options: Someone who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy, but when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, immediately stumbles
A person who loves money above God
explanation: He who received seed on stony places hears the word with joy, yet has no root in himself and quickly falls away when trials come.

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the good soil represent?
options: A person who hears the word, understands it, keeps it, and bears fruit with patience
Someone who is born into a righteous family
A scholar of the Mosaic law
explanation: Good ground represents noble and good hearts who hear the word, hold it fast, and bear fruit with endurance.

question: In the Parable of the Two Sons in Matthew 21, whom did Jesus say enters the kingdom of God before the hypocritical religious leaders?
explanation: Jesus said to them: 'Assuredly, I say to you that tax collectors and harlots enter the kingdom of God before you.'

question: In the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers, what does the landowner do to the wicked vinedressers after they murder his beloved son?
options: He destroys those wicked men miserably and leases his vineyard to other vinedressers who will render him the fruits in their seasons
He abandons the vineyard to ruin
explanation: The religious leaders themselves answered: 'He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and lease his vineyard to other vinedressers.'

question: Immediately after the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers, which messianic Psalm does Jesus quote concerning the rejected stone?
explanation: Jesus quoted Psalm 118: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone. This was the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes.'

question: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector, in what manner did the Pharisee pray in the temple?
options: Stood and prayed thus with himself, boasting of his fasting twice a week and giving tithes of all he possessed
explanation: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself: 'God, I thank You that I am not like other men... I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I possess.'

question: In Luke 18:14, what was the verdict on the two men praying in the temple?
options: The tax collector went down to his house justified rather than the other
explanation: Jesus declared: 'I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.'

question: In the Parable of the New Wine in Old Wineskins, what happens if new wine is put into old, brittle wineskins?
options: The new wine bursts the wineskins, the wine is spilled, and the skins are ruined
The old skins become soft again
explanation: New fermenting wine bursts brittle old wineskins, ruining both wine and skins; new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.

question: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep in Luke 15, what does the rejoicing shepherd do when he finds his lost sheep?
options: Lays it on his shoulders rejoicing and calls friends and neighbors to celebrate
Leaves it at a stranger's pen
explanation: When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing, and says to his neighbors: 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!'

question: According to Luke 15:7 and 15:10, what takes place in heaven when one single sinner repents on earth?
options: Joy in the presence of the angels of God
explanation: Jesus said: 'There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.'

question: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard, what complaint did the early morning workers voice when receiving their one denarius pay?
options: They wanted to be paid in gold
They complained that the owner made those who worked only one hour equal to them who bore the burden and heat of the day
The owner shortchanged them by five coins
explanation: They grumbled: 'These last men have worked only one hour, and you made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the heat of the day.'

question: What reply did the vineyard owner give to the grumbling workers in Matthew 20:13-15?
options: 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Is your eye evil because I am good?'
'I will give you an extra coin tomorrow'
explanation: He replied: 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong... Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with my own things? Or is your eye evil because I am good?'

question: In the Parable of the Net (Dragnet) in Matthew 13:49-50, how will the end of the age resemble the sorting of fish?
options: The angels will come forth, separate the wicked from among the just, and cast them into the furnace of fire
The sea will dry up completely
The fish will be weighed on a scale
explanation: The angels will separate the wicked from among the just and cast them into the furnace of fire where there will be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

question: In the Sheep and Goats judgment, for whom was the 'everlasting fire' originally prepared?
explanation: Jesus will say to those on the left: 'Depart from Me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.'

question: In the Sheep and Goats judgment in Matthew 25:40, what is the King's criterion for ministry rendered to Him?
options: 'Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me'
explanation: The King will answer: 'Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.'

question: In the Parable of the Householder in Matthew 13:52, what does every scribe instructed concerning the kingdom of heaven bring out of his treasure?
explanation: He is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.

question: In the Parable of the Unmerciful Servant, when the king heard what his forgiven servant had done to his fellow debtor, what did he do?
options: Shrugged it off as human nature
Delivered him to the torturers/jailers until he should pay all that was due to him
explanation: His master was angry, and delivered him to the torturers until he should pay all that was due to him.

question: What solemn warning does Jesus attach to the end of the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant in Matthew 18:35?
options: 'So My heavenly Father also will do to you if each of you, from his heart, does not forgive his brother his trespasses'
'Debts must always be collected on time'
explanation: Jesus warned: 'So My heavenly Father also will do to you if each of you, from his heart, does not forgive his brother his trespasses.'

question: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, when the foolish virgins returned from buying oil and knocked on the closed bridal door, what did the bridegroom say?
options: 'Assuredly, I say to you, I do not know you'
explanation: He answered and said, 'Assuredly, I say to you, I do not know you.' Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

question: In Ezekiel 17, what allegorical creatures feature in the parable of the cedar tree and the vine?
explanation: Ezekiel 17 presents the parable of two great eagles representing the kings of Babylon (Nebuchadnezzar) and Egypt (Pharaoh Hophra).

question: In Ezekiel 24, what object is used as a parable to symbolize the bloody city of Jerusalem about to face the furnace of Babylonian siege?
options: A boiling cooking pot (caldron) full of choice meat and bones set upon the coals
explanation: God commanded Ezekiel: 'Set on a pot... put the pieces into it... Wo to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is in it!'

question: In Luke 8, where does a lamp belong according to Jesus' parabolic teaching on light?
options: Under a bed or covered with a vessel
On a lampstand, so those who enter may see the light
explanation: No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed, but sets it on a lampstand, that those who enter may see the light.

question: In Luke 15, what animal did the father command to be killed to prepare a celebration feast for the returned prodigal son?
explanation: The father commanded: 'And bring the fatted calf here and kill it, and let us eat and be merry; for this my son was dead and is alive again.'

question: Which of the four Gospels contains NO narrative story-parables such as the Sower, the Prodigal Son, or the Good Samaritan?
explanation: The Gospel of John contains allegories and metaphors (the Good Shepherd, the True Vine) but not a single narrative story-parable (parabole) found in the Synoptics.

question: Which Gospel contains the greatest number of unique parables found nowhere else, including the Good Samaritan, the Prodigal Son, and the Rich Fool?
reference: Gospel of Luke ('Special Luke' / L Source)
explanation: Luke contains the highest number of unique parables (around 18 unique parables, including Prodigal Son, Good Samaritan, Rich Man and Lazarus, Pharisee & Tax Collector).

question: What is the ONLY proper name given to an earthly character inside any of Jesus' narrative parables in the Gospels?
explanation: Lazarus (meaning 'God has helped' in Hebrew) is the only personal name ever assigned to a human character in any of Jesus' parables.

question: In the Parable of the Unjust Steward in Luke 16, what were the exact original debts and the discounted amounts written down by the debtors?
options: 100 measures of oil discounted to 50, and 100 measures of wheat discounted to 80
500 measures of barley to 300, and 20 measures of wine to 10
100 talents of silver to 50, and 200 denarii to 100
70 jars of honey to 40, and 100 loaves to 50
explanation: The debtor owing a hundred measures of oil wrote fifty; the debtor owing a hundred measures of wheat wrote eighty.

question: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard (Matthew 20), at what five distinct hours of the day did the landowner go out to hire workers?
options: Early morning (6 AM), 3rd hour (9 AM), 6th hour (12 PM), 9th hour (3 PM), and 11th hour (5 PM)
1st hour, 2nd hour, 3rd hour, 4th hour, and 5th hour
explanation: The householder hired laborers early in the morning, at the third hour, sixth hour, ninth hour, and eleventh hour (one hour before sunset).

question: What specific weed or toxic grass in the Middle East is known as 'tares' (Greek zizania) in the Parable of the Wheat and Tares, closely resembling wheat until heading?
explanation: Zizania refers to bearded darnel, a poisonous mimic grass that looks identical to wheat until ears appear, whose grain produces vertigo if eaten.

question: In 2 Samuel 14, what parabolic story did the wise woman of Tekoa tell King David at Joab's instigation to convince him to bring back his exiled son Absalom?
options: A story about two fighting brothers where one killed the other, and the family demanded the execution of her only remaining heir
A story about a lost camel
A story about a thief in a vineyard
A story of an ungrateful king
explanation: She pretended to be a widow whose son killed his brother in a field fight; the clan's demand to put the surviving heir to death would quench her dead husband's last ember.

question: In the Parable of the Faithful and Wise Servant in Matthew 24:51, what gruesome fate does the master assign to the hypocritical servant who beat his fellow servants and ate with drunkards?
options: Cast him into the Dead Sea
Cut him in two (dichotomize him) and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites
Blind his eyes and make him grind corn
explanation: The master 'will cut him in two and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth' (Greek dichotomeo).

question: In the Parable of the Minas in Luke 19, what terrifying decree does the returning king give at the end regarding his rebel citizens who said, 'We will not have this man to reign over us'?
options: 'Bring here those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, and slay them before me'
explanation: The newly crowned king commands: 'Bring here those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, and slay them before me.'

question: In the Parable of the Wedding Feast in Matthew 22, when the original invitees treated the king's invitation with disdain and killed his messengers, what military retribution did the king send?
options: He hired a company of archers
He sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city
He placed them under a 40-day siege
He withdrew all water from their wells
explanation: When the king heard about it, he was furious; he sent out his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city (prophetic of Jerusalem's fall in AD 70).

question: In the Parable of the Sower, the Hebrew or Aramaic word 'parable' corresponds to the Hebrew word 'Mashal'. What does Mashal literally mean?
options: A comparison, proverb, riddle, or symbolic representation
explanation: The Hebrew 'Mashal' encompasses proverbs, riddles, allegories, and similes that cast spiritual truths alongside earthly illustrations.

question: In Luke 16, what were the rich man's clothing materials described in the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus?
options: Clothed in purple and fine linen, faring sumptuously every day
explanation: There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple (regal imperial dye) and fine linen (costly Egyptian byssus), feasting luxuriously every day.

question: In Luke 16:26, what geographic and metaphysical reality did Abraham describe that separates the righteous in paradise from the wicked in torment?
options: A great gulf / chasm fixed, so that no one can cross from one side to the other
A gate locked with seven seals
explanation: Abraham said: 'Beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.'

question: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, what did the wise virgins reply when the foolish begged them: 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out'?
options: 'No, lest there should not be enough for us and you; but go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves'
explanation: The wise answered, 'No, lest there should not be enough for us and you; but go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.'

question: In the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25, what harsh accusation did the one-talent servant make against his master?
options: 'Lord, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you have not sown, and gathering where you have not scattered seed'
'Lord, you never gave me enough time'
'Lord, you favored the five-talent servant unjustly'
explanation: He said: 'Lord, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you have not sown, and gathering where you have not scattered seed. And I was afraid, and went and hid your talent.'

question: In Matthew 25:26-27, how did the master turn the wicked servant's own excuse back on him?
options: 'You knew that I reap where I have not sown? Then you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I would have received back my own with interest'
'You should have given it to your brother'
explanation: The master exposed his sloth: If you truly believed I was exacting, you should at minimum have put the funds in the bank to collect interest.

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, when the elder son complained that he had served his father for many years without ever disobeying, what complaint did he make about meat?
options: 'You never gave me even a young goat that I might make merry with my friends'
'You never invited me to eat lamb'
explanation: He complained: 'Yet you never gave me a young goat, that I might make merry with my friends. But as soon as this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him.'

question: What tender response did the father give to the elder brother in Luke 15:31?
options: 'Son, you are always with me, and all that I have is yours'
'Tomorrow I will buy you three goats'
'Depart from my house if you will not celebrate'
explanation: The father comforted him: 'Son, you are always with me, and all that I have is yours. It was right that we should make merry and be glad, for your brother was dead and is alive again.'

question: In the Parable of the Friend at Midnight in Luke 11:8, on what grounds does Jesus say the friend in bed will eventually arise and give him as many loaves as he needs?
options: Because of their deep boyhood friendship
Because of his persistence / shameless audacity (anaideia)
Because his children woke up crying
Because the bread was spoiling anyway
explanation: Jesus said: 'Yet because of his persistence (Greek anaideia: shamelessness, impudence), he will rise and give him as many as he needs.'

question: In the Parable of the Unmerciful Servant, roughly how many days of manual labor wages did 100 denarii represent in Roman antiquity?
options: About 100 days' wages (roughly three months of hard labor)
explanation: A denarius was standard daily wage for a laborer; 100 denarii represented roughly three months' wages, dwarfed completely by the 10,000 talents (millions of days).

question: In Matthew 13, Jesus quotes Isaiah 6:9-10 to explain why He speaks to hardened crowds in parables. What did Isaiah prophesy?
options: 'Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive; for the hearts of this people have grown dull'
'They will love the truth more than silver'
explanation: Isaiah foresaw judicial blinding: 'For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, and their eyes they have closed.'

question: In the Parable of the Leaven in Matthew 13:33, roughly how much grain was represented by 'three measures' (seahs) of meal?
options: About an ephah (roughly 22 liters or over 50 pounds of flour, enough to bake bread for over a hundred people)
explanation: Three seahs equaled one ephah (approx. 22 liters or roughly 50 lbs of flour), a massive feast portion echoing Sarah's hospitality in Genesis 18:6.

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, down what notoriously dangerous road was the traveler journeying when thieves ambushed him?
options: From Jerusalem to Jericho ('The Way of Blood')
explanation: The 17-mile descent from Jerusalem to Jericho dropped over 3,000 feet through winding, rocky gorges notoriously infested by bandits (the Ascent of Adummim).

question: In the Parable of the Sower, which Gospel specifically adds that when the seed fell on the rock, it withered 'because it lacked moisture'?
explanation: Luke 8:6 uniquely notes: 'And some fell on rock; and as soon as it sprang up, it withered away because it lacked moisture.'

question: In 1 Kings 20, what prophetic parable did a wounded prophet stage before King Ahab of Israel to convict him for sparing Ben-Hadad, king of Syria?
options: A story of a guard entrusted with a prisoner who escaped while the guard 'was busy here and there'
A fable of an eagle catching a serpent
A story of a shepherd losing a lamb to wolves
explanation: The prophet disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes, claiming a prisoner escaped while he was busy here and there, forcing Ahab to pronounce his own doom.

question: In Ezekiel 19, what two animals are used as poetic metaphors for the princes of Judah who were captured in pits and carried off in chains?
explanation: Ezekiel took up a lamentation for Judah's princes, describing a mother lioness rearing young lions (Jehoahaz and Jehoiachin) who learned to catch prey and were captured.

question: In the Parable of the Barren Fig Tree in Luke 13, what did the tree do to the soil that made the owner say 'cut it down'?
options: It cumbered the ground / used up the soil nutrients needlessly without fruit
explanation: The owner says, 'Cut it down; why does it use up (cumber) the ground?' (Greek katargei: depleting moisture and nutrients fruitlessly).

question: In the Parable of the Two Debtors in Luke 7, what three traditional acts of hospitality did Simon the Pharisee fail to give Jesus, which the weeping sinful woman fulfilled with tears and perfume?
options: Water for His feet, a kiss of greeting, and anointing His head with oil
A warm cloak, a silver bowl, and sweet bread
A seat of honor, washing His hands, and singing a psalm
A cup of wine, figs, and an escort to the door
explanation: Jesus said: 'You gave Me no water for My feet, but she has washed My feet with her tears... You gave Me no kiss... You did not anoint My head with oil, but this woman has anointed My feet with fragrant oil.'

question: In the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers in Luke 20:18, what solemn warning does Jesus declare concerning the Chief Cornerstone?
options: 'Whoever builds upon it will conquer Rome'
'Whoever falls on that stone will be broken; but on whomever it falls, it will grind him to powder'
explanation: Jesus warned: 'Whoever falls on that stone will be broken; but on whomever it falls, it will grind him to powder.'

question: In the Parable of the Rich Fool in Luke 12, what phrase does Jesus use to summarize the tragedy of accumulating earthly fortune without spiritual devotion?
options: 'He who gathers gold loses his mind'
'So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God'
'Wealth is the root of all sadness'
'The barns of the earth fade away'
explanation: Jesus concluded: 'So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.'

question: In Matthew 13:51, after teaching the parables of the Sower, Tares, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Treasure, Pearl, and Dragnet, what direct question did Jesus ask His disciples?
options: 'Can you explain these to the Pharisees?'
'Do you have oil in your vessels?'
explanation: Jesus said to them, 'Have you understood all these things?' They said to Him, 'Yes, Lord.'

question: In Luke 14:12-14, whom does Jesus tell His host to invite when giving a dinner or banquet, rather than friends, brothers, relatives, or rich neighbors?
options: The poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind, who cannot repay you
explanation: He said to invite the poor, crippled, lame, and blind, for they cannot repay you, but you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just.

question: In Matthew 25, in the Parable of the Ten Virgins, what did all ten virgins do while the bridegroom was delayed?
options: They prayed all night without stopping
They quarreled over whose lamp was brightest
They went back to their homes
explanation: Matthew 25:5 explicitly records that 'while the bridegroom was delayed, they all slumbered and slept'—both the wise and the foolish fell asleep.

question: In Luke 15, which Greek coins were the ten pieces of silver that the woman owned in the Parable of the Lost Coin?
explanation: Luke specifies ten 'drachmas' (drachmai), each equivalent to a Roman denarius (one day's wage), often strung together as a bridal headdress.

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, to which city was the traveler going down from Jerusalem?
explanation: Jesus answered: 'A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves.'

question: In the Parable of the Sheep and Goats, what six specific charitable acts toward the needy are commended by the King?
options: Feeding the hungry, giving drink to the thirsty, welcoming the stranger, clothing the naked, visiting the sick, and coming to those in prison
Fasting, tithing, praying at noon, giving alms at the temple, building a synagogue, and reading scrolls
Building hospitals, writing books, freeing slaves, paying taxes, planting trees, and burying the dead
Singing psalms, washing feet, weeping for Zion, wearing sackcloth, anointing priests, and fighting enemies
explanation: The six works of mercy: fed when hungry, gave drink when thirsty, sheltered when a stranger, clothed when naked, visited when sick, visited when in prison.

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, into what kind of country did the younger son travel after gathering all his inheritance together?
explanation: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, journeyed to a far country, and there wasted his possessions with prodigal living.

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what pods or husks was the starving youth longing to eat in the pig pen?
explanation: The Greek 'keratia' refers to the horn-shaped pods of the carob tree, commonly used in ancient times as fodder for pigs and cattle.

question: In Luke 15:17, what key turning point phrase marks the beginning of the prodigal son's repentance?
explanation: Luke 15:17 states: 'But when he came to himself, he said: How many of my father's hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!'

question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what planned confession did the younger son rehearse in his heart before meeting his father?
options: 'Father, give me another chance with money'
'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants'
'Father, the famine ruined me through no fault of my own'
'Father, let me work for my elder brother'
explanation: He resolved to say: 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.'

question: In the Parable of the Two Sons in Matthew 21, what did the second son say when his father commanded him to work in the vineyard, and what did he do?
options: He said 'I will not,' but later went
He answered, 'I go, sir,' but did not go
He threw down his tools and fled
explanation: He answered and said, 'I go, sir,' but he did not go, symbolizing religious hypocrisy that pledges verbal obedience without doing God's will.

question: In Matthew 13:35, which Old Testament prophetic psalm is cited to explain Jesus speaking in parables ('I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things kept secret from the foundation of the world')?
explanation: Matthew cites Asaph in Psalm 78:2: 'I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old.'

question: In Luke 12:35-37, what will the master do for his watchful servants who are ready and waiting when he returns from the wedding?
options: Gird himself, have them sit down to eat, and come and serve them
Appoint them as governors of Judea
Give them ten days of rest
explanation: In an astounding reversal of status, the master will gird himself, have his faithful servants recline at table, and come and serve them.

question: In the Parable of the Talents, what is the master's joyful commendation spoken to BOTH the five-talent and two-talent servants?
options: 'Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord'
'Take half of my estate as an inheritance'
explanation: Both faithful servants receive the exact same praise and invitation: 'Well done, good and faithful servant... enter into the joy of your lord.'

question: In the Parable of the Patch on an Old Garment in Luke 5:36, why does no one tear a piece from a new garment to patch an old one?
options: The new cloth fades too quickly
The new cloth makes a tear in the new, and the piece from the new does not match the old
The old cloth will catch fire
explanation: If he does, the new piece tears the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

question: In Matthew 7:3-5, what common construction items are used in the parabolic warning against hypocritical judgment?
options: A speck in your brother's eye and a plank (beam/log) in your own eye
A brick and a mortar trowel
explanation: Jesus asks: 'And why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but do not consider the plank in your own eye?'

question: In Matthew 7:6, to what animals does Jesus warn disciples not to cast what is holy or their pearls, lest they trample them and tear you in pieces?
explanation: Jesus said: 'Do not give what is holy to the dogs; nor cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you in pieces.'

question: In the Parable of the Children in the Marketplace in Luke 7:31-35, what did the children complain that their peers would not do?
options: 'We built a wall and you did not defend it'
'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we mourned to you, and you did not weep'
'We brought bread and you would not eat'
'We ran a race and you would not run'
explanation: They say: 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we mourned to you, and you did not weep,' illustrating the stubborn generation that rejected both John the Baptist and Jesus.

question: In Luke 16:9, what paradoxical instruction does Jesus give concerning worldly wealth following the Parable of the Unjust Steward?
options: 'Burn all silver in the temple fire'
'Make friends for yourselves by unrighteous mammon, that when you fail, they may receive you into an everlasting home'
explanation: Jesus instructs believers to use earthly wealth shrewdly for eternal kingdom purposes, converting temporal mammon into everlasting friendships in heaven.

question: In the Parable of the Vine and the Branches in John 15, what does the Vinedresser (the Father) do to every branch in Christ that does not bear fruit, and what does He do to every branch that bears fruit?
options: He paints the fruitless and waters the fruitful
He takes away every branch that does not bear fruit; and every branch that bears fruit He prunes, that it may bear more fruit
He grafts in wild olive shoots
explanation: Jesus declared: 'Every branch in Me that does not bear fruit He takes away; and every branch that bears fruit He prunes, that it may bear more fruit.'
